安道全，绰号「神医」，建康府人氏。其人医道精通，针灸药石，无所不晓，凡疑难重症、.en:
An Daoquan, known as the Divine Physician, came from Jiankang Prefecture. He was versed in every branch of medicine, from acupuncture to drugs and mineral remedies. Difficult illnesses, severe disorders, abscesses and ulcers, internal injuries and ailments contracted from outside all yielded remarkable results under his care. Throughout the martial world he was therefore respectfully called the Divine Physician. His skill could stand beside that of the ancient masters Bian Que and Hua Tuo, whose hands restored the dying to health, and his reputation spread far and wide.

An Daoquan had originally been a respected doctor in Jiankang, running an apothecary and treating the sick. He had no connection with Liangshan Marsh until a grave illness struck Song Jiang. The Liangshan heroes had defeated Gaotangzhou and Huazhou and were gaining renown. After receiving heavenly books at the Temple of the Mystic Lady and leading an attack on Zengtou Market, Song Jiang was exhausted by campaigning. A malignant sore erupted on his back; the infection grew dangerous, his whole body became red and swollen, and he could take neither food nor water. His life was in peril, and the doctors in the stronghold could do nothing. Dai Zong, the Marvelous Traveler, anxiously sought renowned physicians without success. Then Zhang Shun, the White Streak in the Waves, recalled that his mother had once been cured by An Daoquan of Jiankang. Such a miraculous doctor, he said, could surely save Song Jiang. Delighted, the chieftains asked Dai Zong and Zhang Shun to travel overnight to Jiankang and respectfully invite him.

They found An Daoquan in Jiankang, but he was then deeply involved with a courtesan named Li Qiaonu. Absorbed in wine and pleasure, he refused to accompany Zhang Shun to Liangshan. Repeated pleas and promises of a handsome reward only brought excuses. While Zhang Shun struggled with this refusal, disaster struck. Li Qiaonu had another lover, Zhang Wang, a hanger-on maintained by the brothel keeper and a villain who murdered for money. One night Zhang Wang killed both Li Qiaonu and the madam and stole their valuables. Zhang Shun stumbled into the affair and nearly became entangled in the prosecution. In desperation he turned the situation to his advantage, writing on the wall in blood: “The murderer is An Daoquan.” This cut off the physician's retreat. Seeing the bloodstained accusation, An Daoquan knew that remaining in Jiankang would bring legal disaster. With no way out, he packed his belongings and fled that night to Liangshan with Zhang Shun and Dai Zong. The episode of Zhang Shun's night of turmoil in Jiankang and his trick to bring the Divine Physician to the mountain introduces An Daoquan and also reveals how far Liangshan would go to recruit talent.

On reaching Liangshan, An Daoquan immediately examined Song Jiang's sore. After carefully assessing it, he used acupuncture, external medicines and restorative decoctions. Over several days the swelling subsided, and in fewer than ten days Song Jiang recovered, regained his spirits and resumed military affairs. An Daoquan remained in the stronghold to treat the chieftains and soldiers for illnesses and battle wounds, with success wherever his care was needed. When the 108 heroes assembled and their ranks were fixed, he was assigned the Earthly Spirit Star and the fifty-sixth seat among the Earthly Fiends. He supervised the physicians practicing both internal medicine and surgery, becoming the army's chief doctor.

After Song Jiang accepted the imperial amnesty, An Daoquan accompanied the army. During the northern campaign against Great Liao and the campaigns against Tian Hu and Wang Qing, sick and wounded soldiers depended on his treatment. He saved countless lives through his medical skill. His eventual fate, however, differed from that of most comrades. As the army prepared to march south against Fang La, the emperor fell mildly ill, and the court physicians could not cure him. Someone recommended An Daoquan's extraordinary abilities. An imperial decree retained him in the capital and appointed him to the Imperial Medical Academy to attend the sovereign. Thus, ordered to remain in the capital, he did not join Song Jiang's southern campaign against Fang La.

Later generations have often remarked upon his good fortune. In the campaign against Fang La, seven or eight of every ten Liangshan heroes were killed or grievously lost, leaving a scene of terrible devastation. By remaining in the capital, An Daoquan escaped that catastrophe intact. Instead of returning wrapped in a horsehide shroud, he received a post at the Imperial Medical Academy, enjoyed his salary and died peacefully in the capital. He was one of the rare members of the 108 to preserve his life and live out his natural years. The healing skills that saved so many Liangshan brothers ultimately saved their owner as well. The name Divine Physician was deserved: his story began well and ended well.
安道全，绰号「神医」，建康府人氏。其人医道精通，针灸药石，无所不晓，凡疑难重症、.ja:
安道全は、あだ名を「神医」といい、建康府の出身である。医術に精通し、鍼灸から薬や鉱物を用いた治療まで、知らぬものはなかった。難病や重病、腫れ物や潰瘍、内傷や外から受けた病も、彼の手にかかればたちどころに効き目が現れた。そのため江湖の人々は、敬意を込めて「神医」と呼んだ。死の淵にある者を救うその腕は、古の扁鵲や華佗にも比べられ、名声は遠近に広く知れ渡っていた。

安道全はもともと建康府で薬屋を開き、病人を救って暮らす良医で、梁山泊とは何の関わりもなかった。彼が山へ入ることになったのは、宋江の大病がきっかけである。梁山の好漢たちは高唐州や華州を攻略し、ますます威名を高めていた。その後、玄女廟で天書を授かり、さらに曾頭市を攻めた宋江は、戦の疲れから背中に悪性の腫れ物を生じた。毒が広がって全身が赤く腫れ、水も食事も受け付けず、命が危うくなった。山寨にも医者はいたが、誰も手の施しようがない。神行太保の戴宗は焦り、名医を探し回ったものの見つからなかった。そこへ浪裏白条の張順が、かつて母の病を建康府の神医・安道全に治してもらったと申し出た。あの医術なら宋江も救えるというのである。頭領たちは大いに喜び、戴宗と張順に、夜を徹して建康府へ赴き、礼を尽くして安道全を迎えるよう頼んだ。

建康に着いた張順と戴宗は安道全を見つけた。しかし彼はそのころ、李巧奴という妓女と深い仲になり、酒と色事に溺れて、張順と山へ行こうとしなかった。何度懇願し、大金を約束しても、安道全は言い逃ればかりする。張順が困り果てていると、思いがけない大事件が起こった。李巧奴にはもう一人の情夫がいた。張旺という、妓楼の女主人に食わせてもらう遊び人で、金のためなら人も殺す悪党だった。張旺は夜中に李巧奴と女主人を殺し、財物を奪った。張順は偶然この事件に巻き込まれ、危うく罪を問われかけた。追い詰められた彼は、この状況を逆に利用し、壁に血で「人を殺したのは安道全なり」と書いて、安道全の退路を断った。血文字を見た安道全は、建康に残れば必ず訴追されると悟り、進退きわまって荷をまとめ、張順、戴宗とともにその夜のうちに梁山へ逃れた。この「張順、夜に建康府を騒がせ、神医を計略で山へ迎える」一件は、安道全登場の物語であり、梁山が人材を得るためには手段を選ばなかったことも示している。

梁山に着いた安道全は、すぐに宋江の背の腫れ物を診た。病状を詳しく調べ、鍼灸を施し、外には良薬を塗り、内には煎じ薬を与えて数日養生させると、腫れは次第に治まった。十日もたたぬうちに宋江は全快し、気力を取り戻して軍務に復帰した。以後、安道全は山寨に留まり、頭領や将兵の病気と戦傷を専門に治療し、負傷者を癒やしては成果を上げた。梁山大聚義で百八人の席次が定められると、地煞の地霊星に応じる第五十六位となり、内科・外科を担う医師たちを統率する梁山軍の主医となった。

宋江が朝廷の招安を受けた後、安道全も従軍した。大遼への北征、田虎や王慶への討伐では、病人や負傷者は皆彼の治療に頼り、救った命は数知れなかった。だが、その結末は多くの仲間とは異なる。大軍が方臘討伐へ南下しようとしたころ、皇帝が軽い病にかかった。宮中の医師たちが治せずにいると、安道全の医術を推す者があった。そこで勅命が下り、彼は都に留められ、太医院に仕えて天子を診ることになった。このため、宋江とともに方臘征討へ向かうことはなかった。

後世、このことを語る人々は、安道全の幸運を嘆賞する。方臘との戦いでは梁山の好漢の十に七、八が失われ、死傷は惨憺たるものだった。都に留まった安道全は災いを避け、馬革に屍を包まれることもなく、太医院の職と俸禄を得て、都で安らかに生涯を終えた。百八人のうち、命を保って天寿を全うできた稀な一人である。梁山の多くの兄弟を救った医術は、最後には自分自身の命をも救った。「神医」の名は実にふさわしく、始めも終わりも恵まれた人生だったといえよう。

白胜者，济州安乐村人氏，水浒一百单八将中一员市井出身的闲汉。其人本是个赌钱使坏、.en:
Bai Sheng came from Anle Village in Jizhou, an idle townsman who became one of the 108 heroes of Water Margin. Originally a down-at-heel gambler and troublemaker, he wandered between villages and market towns, doing small business carrying wine and selling drinks while also stealing poultry, cheating and swindling. He was a disreputable street rogue. Lazy by nature, he crept about in broad daylight pursuing dubious livelihoods with the furtive movements of a rat. People in the martial world therefore gave him the nickname Daylight Rat. “Daylight” meant the full light of day; a rat was a thieving creature that hid by day and slipped out at night to steal. Calling him a Daylight Rat precisely captured a layabout who dared sneak and steal even under the sun. The name was hardly imposing, but it portrayed his sly, dishonest habits with piercing accuracy.

Bai Sheng was not a celebrated figure in Water Margin, yet he played a part in one enormous affair: the clever seizure of the birthday gifts. When Chao Gai, Wu Yong, Gongsun Sheng, Liu Tang and the three Ruan brothers planned to rob the gifts worth one hundred thousand strings of cash that Secretary Liang was sending to Grand Tutor Cai in the Eastern Capital, Wu Yong recommended Bai Sheng for a vital role in the scheme. Yang Zhi was escorting the convoy through Yellow Mud Ridge in the fierce heat of the sixth month, and the soldiers were desperately thirsty. Disguised as a village wine seller, Bai Sheng slowly climbed the ridge with two buckets of white wine, singing a country song, and rested in the pine grove. The soldiers wanted to buy a drink, but he deliberately raised objections and pretended to refuse. Wu Yong and the others, posing as date merchants, first bought and drank one bucket. Then they made a show of snatching wine from the other while Bai Sheng was supposedly off guard, secretly adding a sleeping drug. Their staged struggle erased the soldiers' suspicions. Unable to resist the men's insistence, Yang Zhi drank a few mouthfuls too. Soon the entire escort lay drugged, and Chao Gai's party carried off the birthday gifts. In this wine-selling trick at Yellow Mud Ridge, an ordinary porter singing a rustic song helped utterly deceive the capable, shrewd Blue-faced Beast Yang Zhi. It was one of the affair's most memorable strokes.

The great robbery was nevertheless uncovered. Ordered to investigate, He Tao followed the clues to Bai Sheng and arrested him. Bai Sheng initially held out, but the evidence was clear and he could not endure the torture. At last he confessed Chao Gai's name, his companions' identities and origins, and the entire course of the scheme. This confession revealed the seven culprits to the authorities and forced Chao Gai's group to fight their way to Liangshan and become outlaws. Bai Sheng himself was prosecuted and imprisoned. Later, once Chao Gai and his companions had established themselves on the mountain, they remembered his services and their old ties. They bribed the necessary officials, rescued him from the Jizhou prison and brought him to join them. At the great assembly Bai Sheng received the one-hundred-and-sixth seat, corresponding to the Earthly Depletion Star. In the army he gathered news, scouted and arranged support: his talent for sneaking and probing was well suited to intelligence work.

After the amnesty, Bai Sheng followed the army through northern and southern campaigns: against Great Liao, then Tian Hu and Wang Qing, and finally Fang La. In the last campaign the dangerous terrain of Jiangnan and Fang La's formidable troops and commanders cost Liangshan grievous casualties, staining the southeast with blood. Bai Sheng met his end away from the battle line. While the army fought its way through Jiangnan, he contracted an epidemic disease on the march. Confined to his sickbed, he never recovered and died in Hangzhou before Fang La's defeat and the victorious return to court. The Daylight Rat who had sold wine and sung a country song while helping steal the birthday gifts spent much of his life on disreputable business. Yet he too followed Liangshan's enterprise across half the realm, only to fall to a passing epidemic on the southern campaign. That idle villager with the wine buckets, who sang so leisurely and later betrayed Chao Gai under torture, ultimately returned to dust as Liangshan's stars scattered. Only his nickname and the old tale of the birthday-gift robbery remained for later generations to ponder, tracing the causes and consequences of that astonishing crime.
白胜者，济州安乐村人氏，水浒一百单八将中一员市井出身的闲汉。其人本是个赌钱使坏、.ja:
白勝は済州安楽村の出身で、『水滸伝』の百八人のうち、町場の遊び人から身を起こした一人である。もとは賭け事や悪さをして暮らす落ちぶれ者で、村や町を渡り歩き、酒を担いで売るような小商いをする一方、鶏を盗み、人をだまし、詐欺を働くことにも慣れた、表立っては語れぬ無頼漢だった。生来怠け者で、昼間からこそこそ怪しい稼ぎをし、鼠のように身を隠して動くため、江湖では「白日鼠」と呼ばれた。「白日」は真昼、「鼠」は昼に隠れて夜に出歩き、物を盗む獣をいう。白日鼠という名は、昼日中にも鼠のように盗みを働く、この町場の閑人の本性をよく表していた。勇ましくはないが、ずる賢く立ち回る姿を実に的確に描いたあだ名だった。

『水滸伝』で白勝の名は大きくないが、天下を驚かす事件に関わった。それが生辰綱の智取である。晁蓋、呉用、公孫勝、劉唐、阮氏三兄弟の七人が、梁中書から東京の蔡太師へ送られる十万貫相当の誕生祝いを奪おうと計画したとき、呉用は白勝を一味に加え、計略の要を担わせた。楊志が生辰綱を護送して黄泥岡に差しかかったのは、六月の酷暑のころだった。兵たちは暑さと渇きに苦しんでいた。白勝は酒売りの村人に変装し、白酒の桶を二つ担ぎ、山歌を歌いながらゆっくり岡へ上がり、松林で休んだ。酒を見た兵たちは買おうとしたが、白勝はわざとあれこれ言い、売りたくないふりをした。棗売りの商人を装った呉用らは、まず一桶を買って飲み、次に白勝の隙をうかがってもう一桶から酒をすくうふりをし、ひそかに眠り薬を入れた。奪い合う芝居によって、兵たちの疑いはすっかり晴れた。楊志も皆の要求に抗しきれず数口飲むと、ほどなく一行は全員薬で倒れ、十万貫の生辰綱は晁蓋たちに奪い去られた。黄泥岡で酒を売って薬を仕込むこの一幕では、山歌を歌うただの酒担ぎが、精明で有能な青面獣・楊志を見事に翻弄した。生辰綱智取の中でも、とりわけ鮮やかな手並みだった。

しかし、この大事件はついに露見した。捜索を命じられた何濤は手掛かりをたどって白勝を捕らえた。白勝は初めこそ耐えたものの、証拠も明らかなうえ拷問に耐えきれず、晁蓋らの姓名や素性、計略の一部始終を白状した。この自白によって官府は七人の犯行と知り、晁蓋たちは梁山へ逃れて山賊となるほかなかった。白勝自身は罪に問われ、牢へ入れられた。後に晁蓋らが梁山で勢力を整えると、彼の功労と旧情を思い、役人に賄賂を渡して済州の牢から救い出し、仲間として迎えた。大聚義で席次が定まると、白勝は地耗星に応じる第一百六位となった。軍中では情報集め、偵察、接応を専ら担当し、こっそり入り込んで探る手腕を諜報に生かした。

招安の後、白勝は大軍とともに南北を転戦し、大遼を討ち、田虎、王慶を平らげ、最後に方臘征討へ向かった。江南は山川が険しく、方臘の配下にも猛将や精兵が多かったため、梁山の好漢は甚大な死傷を出し、東南の地は血に染まった。だが白勝の最期は、戦場の正面ではなく、行軍中の病だった。江南を転戦する途上で疫病にかかり、病床から起き上がることなく杭州で死んだ。方臘が平定され、軍が都へ凱旋する日を迎えることはできなかった。酒を売り、山歌を歌って生辰綱を奪う手助けをした白日鼠は、世間に誇れぬ仕事の多い一生を送った。それでも梁山の大業に従って天下の半ばを転戦し、最後には流行り病によって江南の旅路に倒れたのである。酒桶を担いでのんびり歌い、後には拷問に負けて晁蓋を白状したあの遊び人も、梁山の星々が散るにつれて塵に帰った。後世に残ったのは「白日鼠」の三文字と生辰綱智取の昔話であり、人々はそれを通じ、この驚天動地の事件の始まりと終わりを幾度もたどるのである。

鲍旭，绰号「丧门神」，寇州人氏。其人生得面目狰狞，凶恶可怖，专一好杀，性如烈火，.en:
Bao Xu, nicknamed the God of Death, came from Kouzhou. His face was hideous and terrifying, and he delighted in killing. With a temper like fire, he would strike at anyone and stop only at the sight of blood: a fiend who killed without blinking. Wielding a broad sword, he fought with exceptional ferocity. Whenever he entered battle he seemed a malignant deity arriving to claim lives, and people in the martial world called him the God of Death. This name belonged to an ancient baleful spirit presiding over death, mourning and disaster. Applied to Bao Xu, it expressed both his savage disposition and his formidable murderous presence.

Bao Xu had originally been an outlaw near Kouzhou. He gathered followers on Withered Tree Mountain and lived by raiding homes and plundering travelers. Withered Tree Mountain was a haunt of Bao Xu and such men as Fan Rui, the Demon King of Chaos, Xiang Chong, the Eight-armed Nezha, and Li Gun, the Flying Great Sage. Xiang Chong and Li Gun later became chieftains of Mount Mangdang and remained friendly with him. Although fierce by nature, Bao Xu greatly respected men of prowess. He and the two men shared the same spirit and became sworn brothers.

Bao Xu's arrival at Liangshan grew out of the affair at Mount Mangdang. Fan Rui, who practiced sorcery, held that mountain with Xiang Chong and Li Gun and declared his intention of swallowing up Liangshan Marsh. Enraged, Song Jiang sent Gongsun Sheng, Lin Chong and other commanders against them. In battle, Gongsun Sheng defeated Fan Rui's sorcery with the orthodox Celestial Five Thunders arts and trapped Xiang Chong and Li Gun in the Eight Formations. After the pair were captured, Song Jiang personally untied them and treated them courteously. Moved by his generosity and righteousness, they submitted to Liangshan and persuaded Fan Rui to do likewise. The three then recommended their friend Bao Xu of Withered Tree Mountain. Xiang Chong and Li Gun knew that beneath his ferocity he was a true fighting man, with extraordinary strength and courage, who could serve Liangshan as a formidable warrior. Song Jiang sent men to recruit him. Bao Xu had long heard of Song Jiang's generosity and willingness to welcome heroes; with Xiang Chong and Li Gun also urging him, he gathered his followers, abandoned Withered Tree Mountain and joined Liangshan. Song Jiang was delighted by his imposing strength and welcomed him. Bao Xu thus took his place among the 108 heroes.

After joining, Bao Xu repeatedly led charges and threw himself into the enemy lines. His ferocity and bloodlust made him a frequent vanguard fighter, breaking formations and cutting down opponents wherever he advanced. With Xiang Chong and Li Gun, whose fighting methods included throwing knives, round shields and javelins, he formed a coordinated and exceptionally fierce assault team. Together they drove back and forth through enemy ranks, a formidable force within Liangshan's infantry. At the great assembly, Bao Xu received the sixtieth seat among the Earthly Fiends, corresponding to the Earthly Violence Star. He served as a valiant shock fighter among the mounted and foot troops. The star's name aptly reflected his violent, bloodthirsty nature.

After the imperial amnesty, Bao Xu followed Song Jiang's army against Great Liao, Tian Hu, Wang Qing and finally Fang La. He fought bravely at the front and earned considerable merit, but his ferocity ultimately brought his death. During the Fang La campaign, the army attacked Changzhou. Song Jiang led troops into the city, where they fought the defenders in the streets. Eager to kill, Bao Xu rushed in ahead of the others, swinging his sword wildly and becoming intoxicated with the slaughter. The opposing commander was Jin Jie, a valiant officer under Fang La, who brought his men to meet the invaders. Amid the confusion, Bao Xu thought only of cutting his way forward. An enemy commander's blade swept diagonally into him while he was unguarded. The God of Death, so fierce throughout his life, was felled by a single blow and died among the struggling troops in Changzhou. Li Kui, the Black Whirlwind, was beside him. Furious at the sight, he drove in with both axes and forced the enemy back. He and Bao Xu had always been close, sharing a bloodthirsty temperament, and Li Kui sought revenge for him. Bao Xu, who had killed countless others, died by the blade himself. He never returned to court with the army or received an imperial honor in life: a lamentable end.

Bao Xu's life began as that of a savage bandit on Withered Tree Mountain. Recommended by Xiang Chong and Li Gun, he joined Liangshan and became known for murderous ferocity, serving repeatedly as a courageous fighter at the head of assaults. The terrible reputation of the God of Death made him seem a life-taking spirit on the battlefield, and enemies trembled at his name. Yet his lust for killing led him to advance recklessly and perish in Changzhou. The violence of the Earthly Violence Star ceased only at death. He stands as one of the fierce warriors among Water Margin's host of dangerous men.
鲍旭，绰号「丧门神」，寇州人氏。其人生得面目狰狞，凶恶可怖，专一好杀，性如烈火，.ja:
鮑旭は、あだ名を「喪門神」といい、寇州の出身である。顔つきは凶悪で恐ろしく、ひたすら殺すことを好んだ。性は烈火のごとく、人を見れば斬りかかり、血を見て初めて収まる、眉一つ動かさず人を殺す凶漢だった。幅広の剣を使い、戦場では並外れて勇猛に戦った。その凶悪さと殺戮への執着から、ひとたび出陣すれば命を奪う凶神が現れたようで、江湖の人々は「喪門神」と呼んだ。喪門神とは古くから死や喪、災厄をつかさどる凶神の名であり、そのあだ名は鮑旭の荒々しい気性と鋭い殺気をよく示している。

鮑旭はもともと寇州一帯の賊で、枯樹山に仲間を集めて山賊となり、家々を襲い、略奪して暮らしていた。枯樹山は、鮑旭や混世魔王の樊瑞、八臂哪吒の項充、飛天大聖の李袞らが拠った場所である。後に項充と李袞は芒碭山の頭領となり、鮑旭とは親しくしていた。鮑旭は凶暴ではあったが、豪傑には深い敬意を抱き、項充、李袞と意気投合して兄弟の契りを結んだ。

鮑旭が梁山へ入ったのは、芒碭山の一件が縁だった。当時、妖術を使う混世魔王・樊瑞は、項充、李袞とともに芒碭山の王を名乗り、梁山泊を併呑すると宣言していた。怒った宋江は、公孫勝や林冲らに兵を率いて討伐させた。両軍が交えると、公孫勝は五雷天罡の正法で樊瑞の妖術を破り、八陣図で項充と李袞を囲い込んだ。計略に陥って捕らえられた二人を、宋江は自ら縄を解き、礼を尽くして遇した。仁義に感激した二人は梁山に帰順し、樊瑞にも降伏を勧めた。三人が加わると、枯樹山の友人・鮑旭を宋江に推挙した。項充と李袞は、鮑旭が凶暴ながらも並外れた力と勇気を持つ好漢で、梁山の猛将となれることを知っていたのである。宋江は枯樹山へ使者を送って招いた。鮑旭も、宋江が義を重んじ、財を惜しまず豪傑を迎えるという評判を以前から聞いており、二人の誘いも受けて兵をまとめ、枯樹山を捨てて梁山へ入った。その威猛な姿を見た宋江は大いに喜んで受け入れ、鮑旭は百八人の列に加わった。

入山後の鮑旭は、たびたび敵陣へ突入し、勇を奮って先頭に立った。凶猛で殺戮を好むため前衛の先鋒を務めることが多く、敵の陣を突き破り、行く先々で兵を斬り倒した。項充、李袞と組み、飛刀、丸盾、投げ槍などを用いる三人は、連携して敵陣を往来し、梁山歩兵の中でもひときわ獰猛な戦力となった。大聚義で席次が定められると、鮑旭は地煞の地暴星に応じる第六十位となり、騎兵と歩兵の中で敵陣に突入して討ち取る驍将を務めた。地暴星の名は、凶暴で殺し好きな彼の性格にまさしくふさわしかった。

朝廷の招安を受けた後、鮑旭は大軍に従って大遼、田虎、王慶を討ち、さらに方臘征討へ赴いた。常に陣頭で勇敢に戦い、多くの功を立てたが、その凶暴さがついには命取りとなった。方臘との戦いで大軍が常州を攻めると、宋江は城内に兵を進め、守備軍との市街戦となった。鮑旭は人を斬ろうと先を争って城へ入り、剣を振り回してはますます殺気立った。そこへ方臘配下の驍将・金節が、梁山軍の侵入を見て兵を率いて迎え撃った。乱戦の中、鮑旭は前へ進んで斬ることに夢中で、敵将が斜めに振るった刀を防げず、まともに受けた。一世を凶猛に生きた喪門神も、一刀で倒され、常州城内の乱軍に命を落としたのである。そばにいた黒旋風の李逵は激怒し、双斧を振るって突入し、敵を退けた。鮑旭と李逵はともに殺し好きで気が合い、以前から親しかったため、李逵はその仇を討とうとした。無数の人を殺した鮑旭も、最後は刀の下に死んだ。凱旋の日を迎えず、生きて朝廷の栄典を受けることもなかった。哀れな結末である。

鮑旭の一生を見れば、枯樹山の凶悪な賊が、項充と李袞の推挙によって梁山に入り、殺戮を好む勇猛さで名を成し、たびたび先頭で敵陣を衝く将となった姿が浮かぶ。喪門神の凶名は高く、戦場では命を奪う神のように恐れられた。だが殺し好きゆえに進み過ぎ、常州城内にその身を失った。地暴星の凶暴さは死んで初めて止んだのであり、『水滸伝』に集う荒ぶる者たちの中でも、一人の猛将であった。

蔡福，绰号「铁臂膊」，上应地平星，梁山泊英雄座次第九十四位。其人本贯北京大名府，.en:
Cai Fu, nicknamed Iron Arm, corresponded to the Earthly Balance Star and held the ninety-fourth seat among Liangshan's heroes. He came from Daming Prefecture, the Northern Capital, and served as chief jailer over its two prison divisions. He handled imprisonment, punishment and executions: the head of the gaol's men who wielded the blades and axes. His brother was Cai Qing, called the Single Flower. Both served in the Daming penal establishment, the elder as chief jailer and the younger as a warder. They earned their living from the government's criminal justice and were accustomed to the bloody edge of the executioner's blade.

Iron Arm suited Cai Fu's profession. He possessed extraordinary strength, with thick arms as hard as iron, and used a heavy executioner's sword. Whenever a condemned man was beheaded in the marketplace, his blade rose and fell cleanly, never missing its mark. The weight and force of that iron-like arm inspired dread, giving him his nickname. Years of prison service had also made him thoroughly familiar with criminal law and the ways of the world. Shrewd and experienced, he adjusted his conduct to the person before him. Although he dealt in life and death, he was not simply a cruel man; he chiefly sought to adapt to circumstances and preserve himself.

Cai Fu became prominent through the case of Lu Junyi, the Jade Qilin. Song Jiang had long admired Lu's reputation and wanted to lure him to Liangshan. He sent Wu Yong to devise a plot, inscribe a seditious poem in Lu's house and have Li Gu report him. Falsely accused of colluding with Liangshan, Lu Junyi was confined in Daming's death row with his life hanging by a thread. This prison was under the Cai brothers' charge. Lu's steward Li Gu, who was already having an affair with his master's wife and wanted him dead, offered Cai Fu a large bribe to kill him in prison. Cai Fu had intended to take the money and carry out the request, but while he hesitated, Chai Jin, the Little Whirlwind, secretly entered Daming on Song Jiang's orders. He found Cai Fu, promised him great riches and repeatedly insisted that Lu must be kept alive. Weighing the stakes, Cai Fu recognized Liangshan's strength and Lu Junyi's destiny as a Heavenly Spirit. He accepted the request, discreetly protected the prisoner and prevented his death in the gaol. Secretary Liang later ordered Lu Junyi's execution several times, but Cai Fu delayed and maneuvered to frustrate it. Lu owed much of his survival to Cai Fu, whose protection was the most consequential good deed of his life.

Liangshan subsequently attacked Daming twice to rescue Lu Junyi and Shi Xiu. On the Lantern Festival night, the heroes coordinated forces inside and outside the city, burned Cuiyun Tower and stormed in, throwing the Northern Capital into turmoil. Caught between the sides, Cai Fu and Cai Qing abandoned their official positions and submitted to Liangshan. As the city fell and bloodlust ran high, Cai Fu performed another great kindness. He sought out Wu Yong and Chai Jin and repeatedly begged them to reduce the slaughter and spare innocent residents. Wu Yong agreed and ordered the army to restrain itself. Countless people in Daming survived because Cai Fu had spoken. This desire to save lives revealed a rare compassion beneath a profession lived by the bloody blade. Thereafter the brothers followed the others to Liangshan.

Because of his long experience in criminal punishment and his remarkable arm strength, Cai Fu was assigned to carry out and supervise executions in the stronghold. Most military death sentences were handled by the Cai brothers, who served Liangshan's penal authority. When the 108 heroes' seats were fixed at the great assembly, Cai Fu was assigned the Earthly Balance Star and the ninety-fourth seat, next to Cai Qing. Both belonged to the Earthly Fiends, one carrying out executions and the other overseeing them, each with his duty.

After the imperial amnesty, Cai Fu served the army against Liao, Tian Hu and Wang Qing. His doom came during the brutal campaign against Fang La in Jiangnan, where so many Liangshan heroes were lost. During fierce fighting around Hangzhou he was killed in battle, dying in imperial service without returning to his native home. The man called Iron Arm had spent his life wielding the executioner's blade and seeing countless prisoners, only to shed his own blood in the south and return in a warrior's shroud. Cai Qing was fortunate enough to survive and make his way home. When Song Jiang returned, Cai Fu was among the fallen officers remembered and honored for their service. He had been a man of Daming's prisons who lived among blades and axes; yet by choosing to protect Lu Junyi and pleading for the city's inhabitants, he showed uncommon mercy beneath those hardened arms. In this he surpassed an ordinary executioner, and readers of Water Margin have reason to pause and sigh at his story.
蔡福，绰号「铁臂膊」，上应地平星，梁山泊英雄座次第九十四位。其人本贯北京大名府，.ja:
蔡福は、あだ名を「鉄臂膊」といい、地平星に応じ、梁山泊の英雄の第九十四位に列する。北京大名府の出身で、当地の監獄では両院押牢節級を務め、牢獄と刑罰、処刑を取り仕切っていた。すなわち牢を管理し、刀斧を扱う処刑人たちの頭である。弟には「一枝花」の蔡慶がおり、兄弟とも大名府の牢城に勤めていた。兄は節級、弟は小押獄で、いずれも官府の刑罰に関わる仕事で食べ、刃の上の血に慣れた人物だった。

「鉄臂膊」というあだ名は蔡福の仕事にぴたりと合う。膂力に優れ、腕は太く鉄のように硬く、処刑用の鬼頭刀を使い慣れていた。市中で斬首を行うたび、刀を上げて下ろす動きは鮮やかで、一度も外さなかった。鉄のような腕から繰り出される一刀は重く力強く、人々を震え上がらせたため、この名が付いたのである。長年牢に勤めた蔡福は、刑法にも世間の人情にも通じた、抜け目なく老練な男だった。相手を見て態度を変えることに巧みで、生殺を扱うからといって一途に残酷なのではなく、その場に応じて身を守ろうとしていた。

蔡福の名が現れるのは、玉麒麟・盧俊義の一件である。宋江はかねて盧俊義の名声を慕い、計略で山へ迎えようとした。呉用を遣わして盧家に謀反の詩を書かせ、さらに李固に訴えさせたため、盧俊義は梁山と通じたと濡れ衣を着せられ、大名府の死刑囚牢へ入れられた。その命が危うい牢を管理していたのが、蔡福と蔡慶だった。盧俊義の家令・李固は、すでに主人の妻と密通し、主人を殺そうと蔡福に大金を贈り、牢内で始末するよう頼んだ。蔡福は金を受けて実行するつもりだったが、迷っているところへ、宋江の命で潜入した小旋風・柴進が現れた。柴進も大金を約束し、盧俊義に手を下さず必ず守るよう、繰り返し頼んだ。蔡福は軽重を量り、梁山の勢力と、盧俊義が天罡星の命を持つことを考えて、保護を承諾した。そしてひそかに世話をし、牢内で命を失わぬようにした。後に梁中書が幾度も斬首を命じた際も、蔡福が間に立って引き延ばした。盧俊義の命が保たれたのは彼の力によるところが大きく、これは蔡福の生涯で最も大切な善行となった。

その後、梁山は盧俊義と石秀を救うため、大名府を二度攻めた。元宵の夜、好漢たちは内外呼応し、翠雲楼に火を放って城へ入り、北京を大混乱に陥れた。乱軍の中で進退に窮した蔡福と蔡慶は、官の身分を捨てて梁山に帰順した。城が落ち、殺気の高まる中、蔡福はさらに大きな善行をした。呉用と柴進を探し、殺戮を少なくし、無実の民をむやみに害さぬよう何度も懇願したのである。呉用は願いを聞き入れ、三軍に節度を守るよう命じた。蔡福の一言で、大名府の無数の人々が命を救われた。人を生かそうとする思いは、日々血の刃を扱う仕事とは裏腹に、稀な仁心を示していた。こうして兄弟は仲間とともに梁山へ上った。

入山後、蔡福は刑罰に慣れ、腕力にも優れることから、山寨で処刑とその監督を専門に担った。軍の死刑執行は多くが蔡福、蔡慶兄弟に任され、梁山の刑罰をつかさどる一員となった。大聚義で百八人の席次が定まると、蔡福は地平星に応じる第九十四位に座り、弟の蔡慶と隣り合った。兄弟とも地煞に列し、一人は刑を執行し、一人は斬首を監督して、それぞれの役目を果たした。

朝廷の招安後、蔡福は大軍に従い、遼、田虎、王慶との戦いに尽くした。そして方臘征討の江南で、梁山の好漢が数多く失われる中、彼にも最期が訪れた。杭州一帯の激戦に加わった蔡福は、不幸にも陣中で戦死し、王事に命を捧げて故郷へ帰ることはできなかった。処刑の刀を握り、数えきれぬ人を見てきた鉄臂膊も、最後には江南に血を流し、馬革に屍を包まれる身となった。弟の蔡慶は幸い生き残り、転戦の末に帰還した。宋江が凱旋し、戦死した将をしのんで功に応じた栄典を求めたとき、蔡福もその中に数えられた。刀斧の間で暮らす大名府の獄吏ではあったが、盧俊義を守ろうとした一念、城中の人々を救った一言には、硬い腕の下にある慈悲が見える。並の処刑人とは異なるその姿に、『水滸伝』を読む者も幾度か嘆息せずにはいられない。

蔡庆，绰号「一枝花」，上应地损星，梁山泊英雄座次第九十五位。其人本贯北京大名府，.en:
Cai Qing, nicknamed the Single Flower, corresponded to the Earthly Loss Star and held the ninety-fifth seat among Liangshan's heroes. He came from Daming Prefecture, the Northern Capital, and was the younger brother of Cai Fu, Iron Arm. Both served in Daming's prison establishment. Cai Fu was chief jailer over the two divisions and handled executions; Cai Qing was a junior warder who helped guard death row and supervise prisoners. Both earned their living from official punishment and were familiar with the blood on an executioner's blade.

His nickname, the Single Flower, had an elegant origin quite unlike the fearsome names of many heroes. Cai Qing had a distinctive habit: he loved to wear a fresh flower beside his temple or on his cap. Although he worked in a prison and practiced the bloody business of guarding condemned men and overseeing beheadings, he was fond of looking handsome and dressing attractively. Whether at an execution in the marketplace or on duty in the gaol, he always wore a bright flower and displayed it openly through the streets. Residents of the Northern Capital, seeing the handsome warder and his habitual ornament, gave him the graceful name Single Flower Cai Qing. Combining toughness with softness, the nickname lent this prison official an unusual air of charm. He lacked his elder brother's astonishing strength, but was agile and skilled with an executioner's sword. The brothers worked well together in administering punishment.

Cai Qing's story mostly follows Cai Fu's and becomes prominent in the case of Lu Junyi, the Jade Qilin. Wu Yong's plot landed Lu Junyi in Daming's death row with his life hanging by a thread. The Cai brothers managed that prison. Li Gu, Lu's steward, heavily bribed Cai Fu to kill his master, while Chai Jin, the Little Whirlwind, secretly entered Daming and offered riches to have him protected. After weighing the consequences, Cai Fu agreed to preserve Lu's life. Cai Qing followed his brother in secretly caring for the prisoner and keeping him alive. When Secretary Liang repeatedly ordered Lu Junyi's execution, the brothers delayed and maneuvered on his behalf. He owed much of his survival to the pair. This was a meritorious act in which Cai Qing followed his brother in doing good.

Liangshan later attacked Daming twice to rescue Lu Junyi and Shi Xiu. On the Lantern Festival night the heroes coordinated an assault from within and without, burned Cuiyun Tower and stormed into the Northern Capital. Caught between the sides amid the fighting, Cai Fu and Cai Qing abandoned their official standing and joined Liangshan. When the city fell and the troops were eager to kill, Cai Fu sought out Wu Yong and Chai Jin and repeatedly begged them not to harm innocent people. Cai Qing supported the plea at his side. Their combined efforts persuaded Wu Yong to restrain the army and spared the city's inhabitants. This concern for life revealed an uncommon humanity beneath the brothers' everyday work in the prisons. Cai Qing then accompanied his elder brother to join the mountain stronghold.

After joining Liangshan, Cai Qing's experience with criminal punishment placed him alongside Cai Fu in the execution service. Most death sentences in the army were carried out or supervised by the brothers, who became officers of Liangshan's penal authority. At the great assembly, when the 108 heroes' ranks were settled, Cai Qing received the Earthly Loss Star and the ninety-fifth seat, next to his elder brother. Both stood among the Earthly Fiends, one executing and one supervising, performing their respective duties in the same service.

Cai Qing was not a mighty commander who independently held a front or led spectacular charges. Nevertheless, he accompanied the army in its wars, answered wherever he was needed and did not lag behind. He served in the two victories over Tong Guan and the three defeats of Gao Qiu. After the imperial amnesty he followed the northern expedition against Great Liao and the campaigns against Tian Hu and Wang Qing, serving in every campaign while remaining beside his brother.

The brutal southern campaign against Fang La cost Liangshan many heroes. Cai Fu was killed in the fighting at Hangzhou, dying in imperial service, but Cai Qing was fortunate enough to survive and return after further campaigning. Escaping blades, spears and arrows, he was one of the rarer Earthly Fiends to reach a peaceful ending. Once Fang La was defeated and the army returned to court, rewards were distributed. Cai Qing could have accepted an official appointment, but the loss of comrades and the parting of brothers by death had disenchanted him with wealth and distinction. Having no wish to serve as an official, he declined honors and returned to his native Daming to spend the rest of his life as an ordinary law-abiding citizen. Single Flower Cai Qing had earned his living amid prison blades and axes, yet retained a personal grace in his love of flowers and fine appearance. He had also helped his brother preserve Lu Junyi and save the city's inhabitants, showing tenderness and compassion beneath a harsh occupation. Compared with Cai Fu's bloody death in Jiangnan, Cai Qing's safe retirement to his birthplace provided one of the Liangshan heroes' more complete and fortunate conclusions.
蔡庆，绰号「一枝花」，上应地损星，梁山泊英雄座次第九十五位。其人本贯北京大名府，.ja:
蔡慶は、あだ名を「一枝花」といい、地損星に応じ、梁山泊の英雄の第九十五位に列する。北京大名府の出身で、「鉄臂膊」蔡福の実弟である。兄弟はともに大名府の牢城に勤め、兄の蔡福は両院押牢節級として処刑をつかさどり、蔡慶は小押獄として死刑囚牢の警備や囚人の監督を手伝っていた。どちらも官府の刑罰の仕事で暮らし、刀の先の血を見慣れた人物だった。

「一枝花」というあだ名には、他の好漢の恐ろしげな呼び名とは違う、風雅な由来がある。蔡慶には、いつも鬢や帽子に一輪の生花を挿すという独特の好みがあった。牢獄に身を置き、斬首の監督や牢番という血なまぐさい仕事をしながらも、見栄えや装いを大切にしていたのである。市中での処刑でも牢内の当直でも、色鮮やかな花を挿して堂々と歩いた。北京の人々は、姿のよい獄吏がいつも花を着けているのを見て、「一枝花」蔡慶という雅号を贈った。剛と柔を併せ持つその名は、刑獄の人にひと味違う風流を添えている。兄ほど驚くべき腕力はなかったが、身のこなしは軽快で、刑刀を使い慣れ、兄と協力して刑罰の務めを果たした。

蔡慶の事績は兄と重なるものが多く、玉麒麟・盧俊義の一件で名が現れる。盧俊義は呉用の計略によって大名府の死刑囚牢へ落とされ、命が危うくなった。その牢を管理していたのが蔡氏兄弟である。家令の李固は主人を殺そうと蔡福に大金を贈ったが、小旋風・柴進も大名府へ潜入し、大金を約束して盧俊義の保護を頼んだ。軽重を量った蔡福が保護を承諾すると、蔡慶も兄とともにひそかに世話をし、牢内で命を失わぬようにした。梁中書が幾度も処刑を命じた際にも、兄弟が間に立って引き延ばした。盧俊義の命が助かったのは二人の力によるところが大きい。これは蔡慶が兄に従って行った善行の一つだった。

その後、梁山は盧俊義と石秀を救うため、大名府を二度攻めた。元宵の夜、好漢たちは内外から呼応し、翠雲楼を焼いて城内へ入り、北京を騒乱に陥れた。乱軍の中で進退に窮した蔡福と蔡慶は、官の身分を捨てて梁山へ帰順した。城が落ち、殺気が盛んなそのとき、蔡福は呉用と柴進を探し、無実の人々をむやみに殺さぬよう繰り返し懇願した。蔡慶もそばで賛同し、兄弟の願いを受けた呉用は三軍を抑えて、城中の人々を守らせた。日頃の刑獄の仕事とは裏腹に、人を生かそうとするその思いには稀な仁心が見える。こうして蔡慶は兄とともに梁山へ上り、仲間となった。

入山後、蔡慶は刑罰に慣れていたことから、兄の蔡福とともに山寨の処刑と監督を専門に担った。軍中の死刑は多くが蔡氏兄弟に任され、梁山の刑罰をつかさどる者となった。大聚義で百八人の席次が定まると、蔡慶は地損星に応じる第九十五位に座り、兄の蔡福と隣り合った。兄弟とも地煞に列し、一人は刑の執行、一人は斬首の監督を受け持ち、それぞれの務めを果たした。

蔡慶は、敵陣に突入して一方面を独力で担う猛将ではなかった。しかし軍の一員として戦いに従い、命じられるまま各所で働き、後れを取ることはなかった。童貫を二度破り、高俅を三度退けた大戦でも軍中で力を尽くした。招安後は大遼への北征、田虎、王慶の討伐に従い、南北を転戦するたびに兄と連れ立って軍務を果たした。

方臘征討の江南では、激しい戦によって梁山の好漢が数多く失われた。兄の蔡福も杭州で戦死し、王事に命を捧げたが、蔡慶は幸い命を保ち、転戦して帰還した。刀槍や矢に倒れず、地煞の将の中では稀に安らかな最期へたどり着いた人となったのである。方臘が平定されて大軍が都へ戻り、功に応じた褒賞が与えられると、蔡慶にも官職を得る道はあった。だが仲間の死傷や兄弟の生き別れ、死に別れを経験して、功名富貴をむなしいものと悟り、仕官する気も失っていた。そこで栄達を辞退し、故郷の北京大名府へ戻り、普通の良民として余生を送った。一枝花・蔡慶は、刀斧の間で暮らす獄吏でありながら、花と装いを愛する風流を持ち、兄とともに盧俊義や城中の人々を救った。厳しい仕事の下には、柔らかな心と慈悲があったのである。江南に血を流した兄に比べ、無事に身を引いて故郷へ帰れた蔡慶の結末は、梁山の好漢の中でも円満なものだった。

曹正者,开封府人氏也。其家世代屠宰为业,本是个杀猪卖肉的屠户。曹正自幼习得一身好.en:
Cao Zheng came from Kaifeng Prefecture. His family had been butchers for generations, and he himself slaughtered pigs and sold meat. From childhood he mastered killing livestock, skinning carcasses, removing bones and cutting flesh. His knife work was so accomplished that meat parted as soon as his hand moved. People therefore nicknamed him the Knife-wielding Demon. “Knife-wielding” praised the sharpness and almost miraculous control of his blade; “Demon” suggested a dexterity and speed as uncanny as a spirit's. Where an ordinary butcher struggled to slaughter a pig, Cao Zheng finished in an instant, hence the name.

Despite his humble trade, Cao Zheng was no ordinary townsman. He had studied under Lin Chong, the Panther Head, and learned fine spear and staff skills. After losses in his butchering business left him without his capital, he wandered abroad and eventually reached Shandong. Near the Wuyue Tower he married a local wealthy man's daughter and settled, supporting himself by his old trade of slaughtering pigs and selling meat. His relationship with Lin Chong was that of pupil and teacher, a connection that later led to a celebrated alliance of heroes.

After his uproar in Wild Boar Forest and rescue of Lin Chong, Lu Zhishen, the Tattooed Monk, burned the Waguan Temple and wandered through the martial world. Hearing that Baozhu Temple on Twin Dragons Mountain offered a strong defensive position and a place to settle, he sought to join its band. But its chief Deng Long would not admit him, leaving him without a refuge. Around this time Lu Zhishen passed Cao Zheng's shop. Seeing a fierce-looking monk with a formidable monastic staff, Cao Zheng questioned him, and they came to blows. He was no match for Lu Zhishen and was at a disadvantage within a few exchanges. Once they learned each other's backgrounds, Cao Zheng discovered that this was the renowned Tattooed Monk. Hearing his account of Lin Chong, he recognized him as an elder of his teacher's generation, bowed and received him respectfully. Yang Zhi, the Blue-faced Beast, subsequently arrived after losing the birthday gifts and finding himself without a way forward. He met Lu Zhishen, and the three planned to seize Twin Dragons Mountain as a home.

The mountain's three imposing defenses were easy to hold and hard to attack. With Deng Long guarding the passes, a frontal assault was impossible. Cao Zheng proposed a stratagem: Lu Zhishen would pretend to be captured, while Cao Zheng and Yang Zhi posed as villagers escorting him in bonds to Deng Long. The ruse would get the gate opened. Deng Long, unsuspecting, admitted them. Once inside, Lu Zhishen suddenly rose, swung his staff and killed him. Yang Zhi and Cao Zheng joined the attack, scattered the followers and took Baozhu Temple. Lu Zhishen became chief, assisted by Yang Zhi and Cao Zheng, and the three held Twin Dragons Mountain as local heroes. Cao Zheng's plan to deceive the guards was crucial and earned him the foremost credit for the capture.

Later, after Liangshan's three attacks on Zhu Family Manor and its attack on Qingzhou, the bands of Twin Dragons, Peach Blossom and White Tiger Mountains united and joined Liangshan. Cao Zheng followed Lu Zhishen, Yang Zhi and the others, abandoning his former mountain for the great brotherhood. At the ranking assembly he received the Earthly Inspection Star and the eighty-first seat. Being a butcher expert in cutting and slaughtering, he was assigned to supervise the construction of large and small warships, and later to oversee the slaughter of cattle, horses, pigs and sheep and the provision of all feasts. Readers should remember that Liangshan numbered tens of thousands who needed wine and meat every day. Such supplies required someone as accomplished in the trade as Cao Zheng. Though seldom conspicuous on the battle line, he was of real importance to the stronghold's logistics.

After the amnesty, Cao Zheng served with the army against Liao, Tian Hu, Wang Qing and Fang La. The final southern campaign brought terrible fighting and countless dead and wounded chieftains. He too failed to escape and was killed in the campaign, dying in imperial service. This Knife-wielding Demon had begun as a Kaifeng butcher. Through chance and fellowship he became Lin Chong's pupil, assisted Lu Zhishen, helped capture Twin Dragons Mountain by a ruse and joined Liangshan in a stirring enterprise. Yet his blood ultimately stained Jiangnan, and he returned wrapped in a soldier's shroud. After Song Jiang's return, Cao Zheng was among the fallen officers granted posthumous honors for their service.

Cao Zheng's origins were lowly, but he had inherited real skill from Lin Chong and was a capable fighter. His ingenious plan for Twin Dragons Mountain showed judgment beneath a rough exterior: he was more than a man relying on the strength of a blade. The talent expressed in his knife work extended to strategy as well as slaughtering animals, giving him his own distinct place among the Earthly Fiends. A butcher who joined the brotherhood, earned merit and left his name in history, Cao Zheng lived up to the name Knife-wielding Demon.
曹正者,开封府人氏也。其家世代屠宰为业,本是个杀猪卖肉的屠户。曹正自幼习得一身好.ja:
曹正は開封府の出身である。家は代々屠畜を生業とし、彼も豚を屠って肉を売る職人だった。幼いころから家業を覚え、家畜を殺して皮を剥ぎ、骨を抜き、肉を切り分ける刀さばきに熟達していた。手が動けばすぐ肉が分かれるほどの腕前から、江湖では「操刀鬼」と呼ばれた。「操刀」は刃を扱う鋭さと神妙な技、「鬼」は鬼神のように測り知れぬ器用さと速さをいう。普通の屠畜人が一頭の豚に手間取る間にも、曹正ならたちまち済ませてしまうため、この名を得たのである。

屠畜人の出ではあっても、曹正はただの町人ではなかった。かつて豹子頭・林冲に師事し、槍棒の優れた武芸を学んでいた。後に家業で元手を失って各地を流浪し、山東へたどり着くと、五岳楼の下で地元の富家の娘を妻に迎えた。そこで落ち着き、再び豚を屠り、肉を売って暮らした。林冲とは師弟の間柄であり、この縁が後に好漢たちの聚義の佳話へつながることになる。

花和尚・魯智深は、野猪林を騒がせて林冲を救い、瓦罐寺を焼いた後、江湖をさまよっていた。二竜山の宝珠寺は地勢が険しく、身を置けると聞いて山寨を頼ったが、頭領の鄧竜は受け入れようとせず、行き場を失っていた。そのころ曹正の店を通りかかり、二人は出会った。曹正は、猛々しい和尚が禅杖を使い、只者ならぬ様子なのを見て問いただし、やがて手合わせとなった。しかし魯智深にかなうはずもなく、二、三合で押し込まれた。素性を聞けば、名高い花和尚・魯智深である。さらに林冲との一件を知り、師の兄弟分に当たる人と悟って、頭を下げて礼を尽くした。やがて、生辰綱を失って行き詰まった青面獣・楊志もこの地へ来て魯智深と会い、三人は二竜山を奪って居場所とする相談をした。

二竜山には堅固な三つの関があり、守りやすく攻めにくかった。鄧竜が関門を守るため、正面からは攻められない。そこで曹正は、魯智深を捕虜に見せかける計略を出した。曹正と楊志が護送する村人を装い、「縛った」魯智深を鄧竜に献じると言って門を開かせるのである。鄧竜は疑わず入れた。関内へ入るや魯智深が突然立ち上がり、禅杖の一撃で鄧竜を殺した。楊志と曹正も同時に動き、手下を追い散らして宝珠寺を奪った。以後、魯智深が頭領、楊志と曹正が補佐となり、二竜山を拠点とする好漢となった。門を欺く策を献じた曹正の働きは大きく、奪山の第一の功だった。

後に梁山が祝家荘を三度攻め、青州を攻めると、二竜山、桃花山、白虎山の三山が力を合わせ、梁山へ帰順した。曹正も魯智深や楊志らに従い、二竜山を捨てて梁山泊へ上り、大義に集った。席次が定められると、地稽星に応じる第八十一位となった。屠畜の出で切り分けに巧みだった彼は、大小の軍船の建造監督を任され、その後は牛馬や豚、羊の屠畜と、宴席の用意をつかさどった。梁山には数万の兵がいて、毎日酒肉を必要とする。これほどの供給は、曹正のように家業に熟達した者でなくては担えない。陣前では目立たなくとも、山寨の兵站では大いに役立ったのである。

招安後、曹正は大軍に従い、遼、田虎、王慶、方臘の討伐に力を尽くした。方臘征討の激戦では、梁山の頭領が無数に死傷した。曹正も乱軍の中で免れず、その遠征中に戦死し、王事に命を捧げた。開封の一介の屠畜人だった操刀鬼は、縁に導かれて林冲の弟子となり、魯智深を助け、二竜山を智取し、ついには梁山に集って華々しい事業に加わった。それでも最後には江南を血で染め、馬革に屍を包まれる身となった。宋江が凱旋し、戦死した将に功績に応じた追贈が行われたとき、曹正もその中にあった。

曹正の一生を見れば、出自は低くても林冲の真伝を受けた、武芸に優れる男だったことがわかる。二竜山を奪う奇策からは、粗野な中にも細やかな思慮があり、刀の力だけに頼る者でないことも見える。刃を操る技は、家畜を屠るだけでなく、人を動かす計略にも通じ、地煞の中で独自の人物となった。屠畜人でありながら大義に集い、功を立て、歴史に名を留めた曹正は、「操刀鬼」の三文字に恥じぬ生涯を送ったといえよう。

柴进，沧州横海郡人氏，乃大周皇帝柴世宗嫡派子孙。当年陈桥兵变，赵宋代周，太祖武德.en:
Chai Jin came from Henghai Commandery in Cangzhou and was a direct descendant of Emperor Shizong of the Great Zhou. After the mutiny at Chenqiao brought the Zhao-Song dynasty to power in place of Zhou, Emperor Taizu, grateful to the Chai family for yielding the realm, granted them an iron certificate inscribed in vermilion and hereditary support. The decree allowed their descendants to invoke the certificate to escape death for an offense. Thus, though descended from a fallen royal house, Chai Jin remained immensely wealthy and distinguished. He loved meeting heroes, upheld righteousness and gave away money freely. Exiled soldiers and men in trouble who reached his estate always received warm hospitality and travel funds, and people in distress often came a thousand li to seek him. His far-reaching kindness moved like the wind, earning him the name Little Whirlwind Chai Jin. With dragon-like brows, phoenix eyes, white teeth, red lips and a three-part moustache covering his mouth, he was an elegant gentleman past thirty, unmistakably a nobleman's son.

His estate was a refuge for heroes in trouble. When Gao Qiu framed Lin Chong and had him tattooed and exiled to Cangzhou, Lin passed through the estate. Chai Jin hurried out to welcome him, entertained him lavishly and gave him silver and letters. Later, when trouble at the fodder depot drove Lin to Liangshan on a snowy night, Chai's support and recommendation again mattered greatly. Before killing the tiger on Jingyang Ridge, Wu Song had spent more than a year at Chai's estate while avoiding trouble. After killing Yan Poxi, Song Jiang first fled to Master Chai as well, and it was there that he met Wu Song in a celebrated encounter. The friendships and beginnings of many Liangshan heroes were bound to this estate. Though not himself leading them in battle then, Chai Jin was an important link among heroes and a hidden supporter of righteous men.

Chai Jin joined Liangshan because of an injustice against his uncle Chai Huangcheng in Gaotangzhou. Prefect Gao Lian, a paternal cousin of Grand Marshal Gao, abused his power. His wife's brother Yin Tianxi coveted Chai Huangcheng's garden residence and tried to seize it, driving the old man to death from anger. On hearing this, Chai Jin went to argue his rights, relying on the iron certificate. But Li Kui lost his temper and killed Yin Tianxi with a punch. Furious, Gao Lian imprisoned Chai Jin, had him savagely beaten and interrogated, and sought his death. Even the certificate could not protect him. Li Kui escaped to report to Liangshan. Alarmed, Song Jiang and Wu Yong raised an army against Gaotangzhou, but Gao Lian's sorcery summoned wind, rain, spirits and demons and repeatedly defeated them. Wu Yong had to bring in Gongsun Sheng, whose orthodox Celestial Five Thunders arts broke the magic. Gaotang fell and Gao Lian was killed. Afterward, the victors could not find Chai Jin: Gao Lian had thrown him into a dry well. Li Kui tied a rope around himself, descended and carried the barely breathing man out on his back. This saved his life. Persecuted by the authorities and unable to preserve his household, Chai Jin committed himself wholeheartedly to Liangshan.

At the great assembly he ranked tenth among the Heavenly Spirits, corresponding to the Heavenly Noble Star, and became one of the chiefs in charge of money and provisions. His imperial ancestry and reputation for generosity gave him high standing in the stronghold, where he was widely respected as a senior leader. Song Jiang's two victories over Tong Guan and three over Gao Qiu further raised Liangshan's prestige. Before the amnesty, around the episodes of Yan Qing cleverly wrestling the Pillar Supporting Heaven and Li Kui impersonating a magistrate in Shouzhang, Chai Jin also traveled in disguise with Yan Qing to the Eastern Capital. There he carried out secret plans amid the Lantern Festival crowds, demonstrating his resourcefulness.

After the amnesty Chai Jin earned merit against Liao, Tian Hu and Wang Qing. During the Fang La campaign he proposed an ingenious scheme: posing as a fugitive under the name Ke Yin, he infiltrated Fang La's court. His refined speech and noble bearing won such favor that Fang La made him an imperial son-in-law, marrying him to Princess Jinzhi. Deep inside the enemy's lair, Chai Jin gathered intelligence. When Liangshan's army arrived, he coordinated with it, lit a signal fire in the palace and turned against his hosts, earning extraordinary credit in the capture of Qingxi and Fang La. Returning to court, he was appointed military commander of the Henghai Army at Cangzhou. Yet he had seen his brothers die and corrupt ministers retain power. As a descendant of the former dynasty, he feared suspicion and eventual disaster. Claiming to suffer a paralytic ailment, he returned his commission and retired as a commoner to Henghai in Cangzhou. There he lived at ease and died in his home region, one of the rare Liangshan leaders who withdrew in time and preserved both life and name. This Little Whirlwind willingly associated with outlaws despite his royal blood, used his family's wealth to aid heroes everywhere, and finally knew when to stop and avoid disaster. Alongside loyalty and righteousness, he displayed a composed and generous breadth of spirit.
柴进，沧州横海郡人氏，乃大周皇帝柴世宗嫡派子孙。当年陈桥兵变，赵宋代周，太祖武德.ja:
柴進は滄州横海郡の出身で、大周の皇帝・柴世宗の直系の子孫である。陳橋の兵変によって趙宋が周に代わった際、太祖武徳皇帝は柴氏が国を譲ったことに感じ入り、丹書鉄券と代々の扶持を与えた。柴氏の子孫が罪を犯しても、この券を示せば死を免れるとの勅令であった。そのため柴進は滅びた王朝の宗室でありながら、大変な富と家格を保っていた。天下の豪傑との交わりを好み、義を重んじて財を惜しまず、落ちぶれた流刑兵や罪を負った好漢が屋敷を頼れば、必ず丁重にもてなし、旅費を与えた。困窮した江湖の人々は、千里を越えて訪ねることも多かった。行く先々に風のように恩恵を施すので、皆は「小旋風柴進」と呼んだ。容貌は竜のような眉、鳳凰のような目、白い歯に赤い唇、口元を覆う三筋の髭を備え、三十を過ぎた風雅な姿から、一目で貴公子とわかる人物だった。

柴進の屋敷は、災難に遭った天下の好漢の隠れ家だった。高俅に陥れられ、刺青を入れられて滄州へ流された林冲が通りかかると、柴進は履物を逆に履くほど急いで迎え、盛大な宴を開き、銀や紹介状を贈った。後に林冲が草料場で難に遭い、雪の夜に梁山へ上った際も、柴進の援助と紹介が大きく役立った。景陽岡で虎を倒す前の武松も、災いを避けて一年余りこの屋敷に滞在していた。閻婆惜を殺して逃れた宋江が最初に頼ったのも柴大官人であり、ここで武松と知り合った話は佳話となった。梁山の多くの英雄の苦難の友情や出発点は、この屋敷と深く結びついている。まだ自ら陣頭に立たずとも、柴進は群雄をつなぎ、義士を陰から支える重要な人物だった。

柴進が梁山へ入る原因となったのは、高唐州に住む叔父・柴皇城の受けた冤罪である。知府の高廉は高太尉の父方の従兄弟で、権勢を頼みに横暴を働いていた。その妻の兄弟・殷天錫が柴皇城の庭園付きの屋敷を欲しがり、無理に奪おうとしたため、柴皇城は憤死した。知らせを受けた柴進は丹書鉄券を頼みに高唐州へ赴き、道理を説いて争った。ところが李逵が激高し、一拳で殷天錫を殺してしまった。怒った高廉は柴進を捕らえて牢へ入れ、激しく打って取り調べ、さらに命を奪おうとした。鉄券さえ守りにはならなかった。李逵は逃れて梁山へ知らせ、驚いた宋江と呉用は大軍を起こして高唐州を攻めた。しかし高廉は妖術で風雨を呼び、神鬼を操り、梁山軍はたびたび敗れた。呉用は公孫勝を呼び、五雷天罡の正法で妖術を破らせて、ようやく城を落とし、高廉を斬った。だが柴進はいくら探しても見つからない。すでに枯れ井戸へ投げ込まれていたのである。黒旋風・李逵が縄を体に巻いて井戸へ降り、瀕死の柴進を背負い出したおかげで、命は救われた。官府に害され、家業も保てなくなった柴進は、心を決めて梁山へ上った。

大聚義では天罡の第十位、天貴星に応じ、金銭と糧秣を管理する頭領の一人となった。皇族の血筋と義に厚く財を施す評判によって、山寨での地位は高く、皆の信望を集める大頭領だった。宋江が童貫を二度、高俅を三度破ると、梁山の威勢はさらに高まった。招安前には、「燕青、智をもって擎天柱を投げ、李逵、寿張で役人を装って裁きをする」ころ、柴進も変装して燕青と東京へ入り、元宵の灯見物に紛れてひそかに策を進めた。その臨機応変な働きも見逃せない。

招安後、柴進は遼、田虎、王慶との戦いに功を立てた。方臘征討では、難に遭って逃れてきた者を装い、「柯引」と名を変えて敵の朝廷に入り込む奇策を献じた。風雅な話しぶりと貴公子らしい気品を方臘に気に入られ、娘の金芝公主を妻に迎える駙馬となったため、虎穴の奥で敵情を探ることができた。梁山軍が迫ると内外で呼応し、宮中に火を上げて合図し、内側から反旗を翻して、清渓攻略と方臘捕縛に大きな功を立てた。凱旋後は横海軍滄州都統制を授かった。しかし仲間が次々に失われ、奸臣が権力を握る様を見たうえ、自身が前王朝の宗室であることから、疑いを受けて災いに遭うのを恐れた。そこで風疾と称して官告を返し、滄州横海郡へ平民として戻った。以後は世を離れて悠々と暮らし、故郷で寿命を全うした。激流の中から時機を見て身を引き、命と名を保った、梁山でも稀な人物である。皇胄の身でありながら草莽に交わり、一門の富を天下の豪傑に分かち、最後には止まるべき時を知って災いを避けた小旋風には、忠義に加え、落ち着いた闊達な風格があった。

陈达，邺城人氏，水浒一百单八将中一员悍勇刚烈的好汉，绰号「跳涧虎」。其人膂力过人.en:
Chen Da came from Yecheng and was a fierce, courageous member of the 108 heroes, nicknamed the Gorge-leaping Tiger. Exceptionally strong, hot-tempered and bold, he was skilled with a steel-tipped spear. On the battlefield he advanced and retreated like the wind, springing and dodging like a tiger leaping across deep mountain gullies. His name described both his swift agility and his untamable courage. In his early years he ran afoul of the law and found nowhere to stay. He therefore became sworn brothers with Zhu Wu, the Resourceful Strategist, and Yang Chun, the White-flowered Snake. They gathered a band on Shaohua Mountain, raiding homes and robbing travelers to the distress of the surrounding countryside. Zhu Wu was calculating and decisive, Yang Chun steady and perceptive, while Chen Da relied on fierce courage and was the most impatient. Each brought a different strength to their mountain band. The authorities offered a reward of three thousand strings of cash for the three chiefs, a measure of their notoriety.

Chen Da's connection to Liangshan began with a bond of generosity involving Shi Jin, the Nine-tattooed Dragon. When money and provisions ran short on Shaohua Mountain, Chen Da proposed attacking Huayin County to obtain grain. Zhu Wu and Yang Chun knew that the route passed Shi Family Manor and that its master Shi Jin was formidable. They repeatedly warned him, but Chen Da trusted his courage and ignored them. Taking roughly a hundred followers down the mountain, he demanded passage through the manor. Shi Jin met him with his spear and captured him alive after only a few exchanges, binding him at the estate. On hearing the news, Zhu Wu and Yang Chun did not abandon their brother. Instead, they employed a self-sacrificing appeal, personally coming to the manor and offering to be bound and delivered to the authorities with Chen Da, to die together and fulfill their oath. Deeply moved that the three valued brotherhood above life, Shi Jin released Chen Da and let the others go. Enemies became friends, and he joined the three mountain chiefs in a bond of life and death. Later, while trying to save someone dear to him, Shi Jin entered Huazhou alone to assassinate Prefect He and was instead captured and imprisoned. The three Shaohua chiefs joined Liangshan's forces in storming Huazhou and rescued him. Afterward Song Jiang warmly invited them all to the marsh, and Chen Da joined Liangshan with Zhu Wu, Yang Chun, Shi Jin and the others.

Once he joined, Chen Da's steel-tipped spear and fierce courage earned him a place among the fighting officers. At the great assembly he received the seventy-second seat and the Earthly Circuit Star. He served as a junior cavalry commander and long-range scouting chief, thirteenth among the scouting commanders. This post required penetrating enemy territory for intelligence before the armies met and then charging in battle, fitting his tiger-like agility and valor. In the wars against Liao, Tian Hu and Wang Qing, he fought shoulder to shoulder with Shi Jin and his old companions, risking his life without ever shrinking from combat.

After the amnesty, Chen Da accompanied the southern campaigns until the war against Fang La brought the army to Yuling Pass. The position was exceedingly dangerous, with two mountains flanking a single narrow path. Pang Wanchun, Fang La's archer known as the Little Yang Youji, and the commanders Lei Jiong and Ji Ji hid a force of bowmen and crossbowmen in the dense woods above the pass, waiting for the Song troops. Unaware of the trap, Shi Jin led Chen Da, Yang Chun and the old Shaohua companions forward as the vanguard and drove into the narrow mountain road. Beneath the pass, a signal suddenly sounded. Crossbows fired from both sides and arrows poured down like rain. Taken entirely by surprise and unable to advance or retreat, Chen Da, Shi Jin, Yang Chun and their comrades were riddled with arrows and died below Yuling Pass, their bodies strewn through the desolate defile. It was a terrible end. The three sworn brothers of Shaohua and the Nine-tattooed Dragon, who had joined Liangshan together and shared life and death, finally died in the same place, their souls returning together to Yuling. When the court later honored the fallen officers, Chen Da received the posthumous title Gentleman of Righteous Integrity for his loyalty and courage. From a fugitive of Yecheng he had become a Shaohua outlaw, been united with Shi Jin through righteousness and joined Liangshan through brotherhood, only to give his life beneath the arrows of the Fang La campaign. The tiger might leap gullies and race through forests, but could not escape that pass's dense rain of shafts. His name and the loyalty of the Shaohua brotherhood remain together in the history of Water Margin.
陈达，邺城人氏，水浒一百单八将中一员悍勇刚烈的好汉，绰号「跳涧虎」。其人膂力过人.ja:
陳達は鄴城の出身で、百八人の中でも勇猛で気性の激しい好漢であり、あだ名は「跳澗虎」という。力が強く、短気だが胆力に富み、点鋼槍を巧みに使った。戦場では風のように進退し、飛び跳ねて身をかわす姿は、深い谷や溝を一跳びに越える猛虎のようだった。この名は、敏捷な身のこなしと、飼い慣らせぬ勇猛な性格の両方をよく表している。若いころ法に触れて居場所を失い、神機軍師の朱武、白花蛇の楊春と義兄弟となって少華山に賊を集め、家々や旅人を襲って近隣を悩ませた。三人のうち朱武は謀略と決断に優れ、楊春は落ち着いて機を読み、陳達はひたすら勇猛で最も気が短かった。それぞれの長所を持ち寄って一党を成し、官府は三頭領の捕縛に三千貫の賞金を掲げた。その勢いのほどが知れる。

陳達と梁山の縁は、九紋竜・史進との恩義から始まった。少華山で金と糧が不足すると、陳達は華陰県を襲って食糧を得ようとした。朱武と楊春は、道中に史家荘があり、その主の史進が強いことを知っていたため、何度も止めた。しかし陳達は勇に任せて聞かず、百人ほどの手下を率いて山を下り、史家荘を通ろうとした。史進は槍を取って迎え、数合もしないうちに陳達を生け捕りにして屋敷へ縛った。知らせを受けた朱武と楊春は兄弟を見捨てず、身を投げ出す苦肉の策を用いた。自ら史家荘へ赴き、陳達と一緒に縛られて官府へ送られ、ともに死んで三人の誓いを守りたいと願ったのである。生死を越えて義を重んじる姿に感動した史進は、陳達の縄を解き、二人も放した。以来、敵は友となり、史進は少華山の三雄と生死をともにする仲になった。後に史進が思いを寄せる者を救おうと単身で華州に入り、賀太守を暗殺しようとして捕らえられると、三人は梁山の大軍と協力して華州を騒がせ、史進を救い出した。事が済むと宋江が熱心に水泊へ誘い、陳達も朱武、楊春、史進らとともに梁山へ上った。

入山後、陳達は点鋼槍と勇猛さによって戦将の列に加わった。大聚義では地周星に応じる第七十二位に座り、馬軍小彪将兼遠探出哨頭領となり、偵察頭領の第十三位を占めた。両軍がぶつかる前に敵地の奥へ入って情報を探り、戦となれば突撃する役目は、跳澗虎のように素早く勇猛な彼に適していた。遼、田虎、王慶との戦いでも、史進ら昔の仲間と肩を並べて死地を出入りし、一度も戦に臆することはなかった。

招安後、陳達は大軍に従って南へ戦い続け、方臘征討では昱嶺関へ達した。そこは両側に山が迫り、その間を一本道が通る険しい関だった。方臘配下の小養由基・龐万春は、雷炯、計稷らと弓弩兵を関上の密林に伏せ、宋軍を待ち構えていた。計略と知らぬ史進は、陳達、楊春ら旧少華山の仲間を先鋒にして進み、狭い山道へ踏み込んだ。関の下まで来ると突然合図が響き、両側から無数の弩が放たれ、矢が雨のように降り注いだ。不意を突かれた陳達、史進、楊春らは進退を失い、乱れ飛ぶ矢を集中して受け、昱嶺関の下でともに死んだ。荒山の険路に屍を横たえる、惨烈な最期だった。かつて梁山へともに上り、生死を誓った少華山の三雄と九紋竜が、最後にも同じ場所で死に、魂を昱嶺へ帰したとは嘆かわしい。後に朝廷が戦死者を追封すると、陳達は忠勇をたたえられ、義節郎を贈られた。鄴城の法を犯した逃亡者から少華山の賊となり、史進の義によって結ばれ、聚義によって梁山へ入り、最後には方臘征討の矢の中で命を捧げたのである。谷を跳び、林を抜ける虎も、その関の密雨のような矢からは逃れられなかった。彼の名と少華山の義気は、ともに『水滸伝』の歴史に残っている。

戴宗，绰号「神行太保」，应天罡之数，乃天速星临世。其人乃江州两院押牢节级，专管牢.en:
Dai Zong, the Marvelous Traveler, was an incarnation of the Heavenly Speed Star, one of the Heavenly Spirits. He served as chief jailer over Jiangzhou's two prison divisions, managing the inmates of its penal camp. His special ability came from a Daoist art called the armored-horse talisman, which allowed him to cover eight hundred li in a day. Before a journey he tied four talismans to his legs and performed his traveling spell. His feet then seemed to ride clouds and mist, carrying him like the wind. This astonishing speed earned his nickname throughout the martial world. He had an imposing presence despite his short stature, a broad face, thick eyebrows, a long beard, black hair and a distinctly Daoist air.

His story opens in Jiangzhou's penal camp. Song Jiang, the Timely Rain, had been tattooed and exiled there for killing Yan Poxi. As the camp's chief jailer, Dai Zong demanded the customary payment. Song Jiang initially took little notice, and Dai Zong was about to punish him. Fortunately, Wu Yong had already written on Song's behalf, and Song Jiang's reputation for righteousness and generosity was widely known. Once Dai Zong recognized him, he eagerly formed a friendship and introduced him to Li Kui, the Black Whirlwind. The three became companions pledged to share life and death, drinking and enjoying one another's company around Xunyang Tower and the Pipa Pavilion in Jiangzhou.

Then Song Jiang, drinking alone at Xunyang Tower, wrote a rebellious poem in his cups. It included threats that one day vengeance would stain the mouth of the Xunyang River with blood and a boast that he dared mock Huang Chao as no true man. Assistant Prefect Huang Wenbing saw it and reported it to Prefect Cai Jiu. Song Jiang was imprisoned and sentenced to death. Cai Jiu wanted to report the affair to his father, Grand Tutor Cai, in the Eastern Capital and sent Dai Zong with a letter. Speeding through the night with his traveling art, Dai Zong stopped at Zhu Gui's tavern near Liangshan and was drugged. The letter found on him revealed an opportunity to save Song Jiang. Wu Yong arranged a forged reply from Cai Jing, with Xiao Rang, the Sacred-handed Scholar, imitating the handwriting and Jin Dajian, the Jade-armed Craftsman, carving a seal. But the seal betrayed them: it used Cai Jing's personal name in a way that exposed the forgery. Huang Wenbing recognized the flaw. When Dai Zong returned to Jiangzhou, he too was jailed and condemned to be beheaded with Song Jiang.

At the execution ground, just before the blades fell, the Liangshan heroes sprang from hiding. Chao Gai led the rescue, while Li Kui charged first with his two broad axes. Amid the confusion they freed Song Jiang and Dai Zong. The heroes fought their way to White Dragon Temple and reunited their forces, then attacked Jiangzhou and Wuwei Military Prefecture. They captured Huang Wenbing alive, cut out his heart and sliced his flesh to avenge Song Jiang. Dai Zong thereafter followed Song Jiang to join Liangshan's righteous brotherhood.

His extraordinary speed made him ideally suited to reporting military intelligence and carrying messages. At Liangshan he became the infantry chief responsible for secret dispatches, reconnaissance and orders, a vital part of the stronghold's eyes, ears and communications. During distant expeditions, rapidly changing enemy movements depended on his swift journeys, setting out in the morning and arriving by evening. At the great assembly, the Heavenly Speed Star received the twentieth seat. Though not distinguished by fighting at the front, his traveling art was one of the army's most important skills. He labored quietly to obtain Gongsun Sheng's assistance, recruit worthy men and discover enemy strengths and weaknesses. He also accompanied Gongsun Sheng home twice and sought out men such as Fan Rui and Tang Long, missions enabled by his speed.

After the amnesty, Dai Zong served against Liao, Tian Hu, Wang Qing and Fang La. In every campaign he continued carrying military intelligence and coordinating scattered forces without failure. He could reach distant mountains in a morning or evening and contributed greatly to the army's movements. He survived the Fang La campaign, despite its dreadful losses among the brothers. After the return to court, he was rewarded with command of the forces at Yanzhou Prefecture. But he had no desire for office. Soon after taking up the post, he returned his commission, bade farewell to his companions and became a resident religious attendant at the Yue Temple in Tai'an. A few months later he died there laughing, passing away seated in spiritual fulfillment. His spirit was subsequently said to manifest at Mount Tai and repeatedly stir within the temple, so local people made an image of him, supported its worship and offered annual sacrifices.

Dai Zong's life combined matchless speed with loyalty and righteousness. He was known less for force than for the strong feet and devoted heart with which he served Liangshan's cause. From helping Song Jiang in Jiangzhou to attaining a blessed end at Mount Tai, his course began and ended well. Few among the 108 could withdraw unharmed and pass seated into immortality. Dai Zong was one: perhaps good fortune indeed accompanied the title Marvelous Traveler.
戴宗，绰号「神行太保」，应天罡之数，乃天速星临世。其人乃江州两院押牢节级，专管牢.ja:
戴宗は、あだ名を「神行太保」といい、天罡の一人、天速星の化身である。江州の両院押牢節級として、牢城営の囚人を取り仕切っていた。特技は、かつて授かった「甲馬」という道術で、一日に八百里を行くことができた。旅立つ際に四枚の甲馬を脚に結び、神行法を行うと、足は雲霧に乗ったようになり、風のごとく走った。その速さから江湖では神行太保と呼ばれた。威のある姿ながら背は低く、顔は広く、眉は濃く、長い髭と黒い髪を持ち、全身に道者らしい気配があった。

戴宗の物語は江州の牢城から始まる。閻婆惜を殺した及時雨・宋江が、刺青を入れられて江州へ流されると、節級の戴宗は慣例の金を要求した。宋江が初め気に留めず、戴宗は罰しようとしたが、幸い呉用からあらかじめ紹介の書状があった。また宋江の義に厚く財を惜しまぬ名は、すでに江湖に広まっていた。相手が宋江とわかると、戴宗は心から交わりを求め、黒旋風・李逵にも引き合わせた。三人は生死をともにする友となり、江州の潯陽楼や琵琶亭の辺りで酒を酌み交わし、楽しく友情を深めた。

ところが宋江は潯陽楼で独り飲み、酔って「反詩」を書いた。その中には、いつの日か恨みを晴らせば潯陽の河口を血で染める、黄巣を大丈夫でないと笑ってみせる、といった句があった。通判の黄文炳がこれを見つけ、蔡九知府へ訴えたため、宋江は牢に入れられ、死罪とされた。蔡九は東京にいる父の蔡太師へ報告しようと、戴宗に書状を持たせた。神行法で夜を徹して急いだ戴宗は、梁山近くの朱貴の酒店で眠り薬を盛られた。見つかった文書から宋江を救う好機と知った呉用は、蔡京の返書を偽造する策を立て、聖手書生・蕭譲に筆跡をまねさせ、玉臂匠・金大堅に印を彫らせた。だが蔡京自身の諱を用いた印に誤りがあり、かえって偽造の証拠となった。黄文炳に見破られ、江州へ戻った戴宗も宋江と一緒に投獄され、斬首を宣告された。

刑場で、まさに刀が振り下ろされようとしたとき、潜んでいた梁山の好漢たちが動いた。晁蓋が一同を率いて刑場を襲い、黒旋風・李逵は二挺の板斧を振るって真っ先に突入した。兵馬が入り乱れる中、宋江と戴宗は救い出された。好漢たちは白竜廟へ走って合流し、さらに江州を攻め、無為軍を破り、黄文炳を生け捕った。そして心臓をえぐり、肉を削いで、宋江の恨みを晴らした。以後、戴宗は宋江に従って梁山へ上り、義の仲間となった。

梁山では神行の能力が軍情の報告や書状の往来に最適とされ、「走報機密歩軍頭領」となった。偵察、情報伝達、号令の伝達を専門に担い、山寨の耳目と喉を支える役目である。遠征で敵情が刻々と変わるたび、朝に発って夕べに着く戴宗の往来が頼りとなった。大聚義では天速星に応じ、第二十位に座った。陣前の斬り合いは得意でなくても、神行法は軍に欠かせぬ最重要の技だった。公孫勝への援助要請、賢者の勧誘、敵情の探索に走り、目立たぬところで功を立てた。公孫勝の帰郷にも二度同行し、樊瑞、湯隆らを訪ねた際にも、その速さが仕事を成し遂げさせた。

招安後、戴宗は遼、田虎、王慶、方臘との戦いに従った。どの遠征でも神行の任務を続け、軍機を伝え、各方面をつないで、一度も失敗しなかった。三山五岳の遠方へも朝夕のうちに達し、大軍の指揮と移動への功は大きかった。方臘征討で梁山の兄弟が甚だしい死傷を出す中、戴宗は幸い無事に生き残った。凱旋後、功により兗州府都統制を授かったが、仕官を志してはいなかった。赴任してほどなく官告を返し、仲間に別れを告げ、泰安州の岳廟で出家の身となって廟を守った。数か月後、廟中で大笑いしながら座したまま往生し、善果を得たという。後に泰山で霊験を現し、たびたび岳廟で動きを示したため、土地の人々は神像を造って供養し、毎年祭った。

戴宗は比類なき速さと、忠義を兼ね備えた一生を送った。勇力よりも丈夫な二本の脚と赤心によって、梁山の大義のため走り続けたのである。江州で宋江を助け、最後は泰山で善果を得たその生涯は、始めも終わりもよかったといえる。百八人のうち無事に身を引き、座化して仙に登れた者はわずかだが、戴宗はその一人だった。「太保」の名には、やはり福縁が伴っていたのだろうか。

邓飞，绰号「火眼狻猊」，乃梁山泊一百单八将之地阖星，三十六天罡七十二地煞之中，居.en:
Deng Fei, nicknamed the Fire-eyed Suanni, was the Earthly Closure Star among Liangshan's 108 heroes. Of the thirty-six Heavenly Spirits and seventy-two Earthly Fiends, he belonged to the latter and ranked forty-ninth overall. A fighting man from the Central Plains, he wielded an iron chain, possessed exceptional courage and had a fierce temperament. Throughout his life he loved combat and placed the greatest value on loyalty to his companions.

Deng Fei had a round face, large ears, a short beard around his cheeks and eyes as red as cinnabar. Their flashing red light made him so imposing that people hesitated to look straight at him. The suanni was said to be one of the dragon's nine sons, a lion-shaped beast mighty enough to devour tigers and leopards. Combining “fire-eyed” with its name described both his red eyes and his lion-like valor. Anyone who saw those eyes widen knew he was a man who disregarded his own life and fought with complete abandon. His fondness for eating human flesh and his impatient cruelty resembled the ways of savages who consumed raw flesh and blood; thus his eyes were always bloodshot, adding to his frightening appearance. His looks and nature suited the reckless, headlong manner in which he fought.

He became an outlaw at Yinma River, a mountain stronghold surrounded by deep hills and thick forests, easy to defend and hard to assault. Pei Xuan and Meng Kang had already gathered a band there. Deng Fei joined Pei Xuan, the Iron-faced Clerk, and Meng Kang, the Jade Banner Pole, raiding households and plundering passing travelers. Each held a chief's place, and they lived freely while dominating the district. Later Yang Xiong, the Pallid Guan Suo, Shi Xiu, the Daredevil, and Shi Qian, the Flea on a Drum, were traveling to Liangshan because of their troubles when they met Yang Lin near Yinma River. Already acquainted with Deng Fei and Pei Xuan, Yang Lin brought them up to meet the band. Together the heroes spoke of Song Jiang's generosity and welcome for talented men, and all longed to go to Liangshan. Deng Fei had heard its righteous reputation and saw heroes from everywhere joining the marsh. He therefore agreed with Pei Xuan, Meng Kang, Yang Lin and the others to gather all their men, money and provisions and join Liangshan together. Song Jiang joyfully welcomed the new heroes with a feast, and Deng Fei took his place among the chieftains beneath the Assembly Hall.

At the great assembly, when the stars' seats were settled, Deng Fei received the Earthly Closure Star and the forty-ninth seat. His duties alongside other commanders included assaulting enemy formations and guarding passes. His particular strength was the iron chain, which he swung as swiftly as a storm, entangling, seizing and smashing his opponents. In battle his fiery eyes glared and the chain flew as he led soldiers forward without fearing arrows or stones. He was a fierce vanguard fighter among Liangshan's foot and mounted forces. In campaign after campaign he coordinated with his comrades, breaking enemy lines or providing rearguard support, and earned substantial military merit.

After Liangshan accepted the amnesty and submitted to the court, Deng Fei served against Liao, Tian Hu and Wang Qing without once retreating from duty. When the court ordered the campaign against Fang La in Jiangnan, he crossed the river south with Song Jiang and fought through Wu and Yue. Fang La held many southern prefectures, commanded numerous troops and generals, and resisted fiercely behind mountains and waterways. Liangshan lost many heroes in the savage fighting, and Deng Fei was among those killed. While fighting in Jiangnan he encountered a powerful enemy commander. He held his ground amid the melee, but was finally overwhelmed by superior numbers and fell at the front, giving his life for the state without returning home. From the brotherhood at Yinma River to the alliance at the marsh and death on the southern expedition, the Fire-eyed Suanni ended his course by shedding blood on the battlefield, true to his lifelong courage and resolve.

After Song Jiang returned, the court remembered the fallen officers. Deng Fei and the other Liangshan brothers who had died in imperial service received posthumous offices, benefits for their families and shrines where later generations offered incense. He was no illustrious Heavenly Spirit, but a rare warrior among the Earthly Fiends. His red eyes expressed a courage indifferent to life and death; his iron chain embodied a lifetime of fighting deeds. Though his name stood among the lower stars, his valor strengthened Liangshan. He remains one of Water Margin's unyielding men, whose formidable presence lingers when the reader closes the book.
邓飞，绰号「火眼狻猊」，乃梁山泊一百单八将之地阖星，三十六天罡七十二地煞之中，居.ja:
鄧飛は、あだ名を「火眼狻猊」といい、梁山泊百八人の地闔星である。三十六天罡、七十二地煞のうち地煞に属し、総席次は第四十九位となる。もとは中原の好漢で、鉄鎖を使い、勇猛さは人に優れ、性格は激しかった。生涯、人と戦うことを好む一方で、何よりも義気を重んじた。

鄧飛は丸顔に大きな耳、頬を囲む短い髭を持ち、両目は丹砂のように赤く光った。その姿は威厳に満ち、人々は直視するのをためらった。狻猊は竜の九子の一つと伝えられる、獅子に似た猛獣で、虎や豹を食うほど強いという。「火眼」と合わせた名は、赤い目と獅子のような勇猛さを表す。江湖の者は、彼が火のような目を見開くと、自分の命を顧みずひたすら戦う男だと知った。もとより人肉を好んで食べ、せっかちで残酷な性格は、生の肉や血を口にする者に似ていたため、目には常に血の色が宿り、一層恐ろしかった。その風貌と気性は、戦場で生死を忘れて突進する戦い方にぴたりと合っていた。

鄧飛が山賊となったのは飲馬川の山寨である。山深く林が密で、守りやすく攻めにくい場所に、すでに裴宣や孟康らが集っていた。鄧飛は鉄面孔目・裴宣、玉旛竿・孟康と結び、家々や行き交う旅人を襲い、それぞれ頭領の地位に就いて、一帯を威圧しながら自由に暮らした。後に、病関索の楊雄、拚命三郎の石秀、鼓上蚤の時遷が、事情あって梁山を目指す途中、飲馬川近くで楊林に会った。楊林は鄧飛や裴宣と親しかったため、一同を山へ案内した。好漢たちは集まり、梁山の宋公明が義に厚く財を惜しまず、賢者を迎えるという評判を語り合い、皆その地に心を寄せた。鄧飛も以前から梁山の大義を聞き、天下の豪傑が水泊へ集うのを見ていたので、裴宣、孟康、楊林らと相談をまとめ、飲馬川の人馬と金糧をすべて整えて、そろって梁山へ入った。宋江は新たな好漢たちを大いに喜び、酒宴でもてなした。こうして鄧飛は聚義庁の頭領の列に加わった。

大聚義で天罡地煞の席次が定まると、鄧飛は地闔星に応じる第四十九位に座った。山寨では他の頭領とともに敵陣への突入や関門の守備を担った。得意の鉄鎖を振るえば風雨のように速く、絡め取り、捕らえ、打ち砕く威力があった。戦場では火眼を見開き、鉄鎖を翻して兵の先頭に立ち、矢石を避けようともしなかった。梁山の歩騎軍の中でも勇猛な先鋒であり、戦のたびに仲間と連携して、敵陣を突き、あるいは殿を守り、救援に回って、多くの功を立てた。

梁山が招安を受けて朝廷に帰順すると、鄧飛は大軍に従い、まず遼、次いで田虎と王慶を討ち、どこでも命を尽くして退かなかった。江南の方臘征討が命じられると、宋江とともに川を渡って南下し、呉越を転戦した。方臘は江南の州郡を占め、多くの兵将と山川の険しさを頼みに頑強に抵抗したため、梁山の好漢はこの激戦で多数失われた。鄧飛も戦死者の一人である。江南で敵の驍将と遭遇し、乱軍の中で退かずに力戦したが、最後には多勢に抗しきれず陣前に倒れ、国のために命を捧げて故郷へ戻れなかった。飲馬川の聚義から水泊の盟約、そして南征での死へと歩んだ火眼狻猊は、生涯の剛勇に恥じず、戦場に血を流して結末を迎えた。

宋江が凱旋した後、朝廷は戦死した将をしのび、鄧飛ら王事に死んだ梁山の兄弟に官位を追贈し、遺族を恵み、廟を建てて祀った。後世の香火を受けることになったのである。鄧飛は天罡の目立つ将ではないが、地煞の中でも得難い猛士だった。赤い双眼には生死を恐れぬ胆力があり、一本の鉄鎖には半生の戦功が刻まれている。名は地煞にあっても、その勇は梁山を力づけた。『水滸伝』の剛直な男の一人として、本を閉じた読者の胸にも、生きているような凜々しさを残す人物である。

丁得孙者，泰州人氏，本东昌府守将之裨将也。生得面颊及项，遍长疤痕，盖少时屡经矢石.en:
Ding Desun came from Taizhou and originally served as a subordinate officer to Dongchang's defending commander. His cheeks and neck were covered in scars, old wounds accumulated from facing arrows and stones since his youth. People in the martial world therefore called him the Arrow-struck Tiger. The name carried two meanings: the arrow scars mottled him like a tiger's stripes, and his nature was tiger-like, refusing to shrink from weapons in battle even when stray arrows struck him. Anyone meeting him would see a fierce face crossed with scars and feel the unmistakable presence of a fighting man.

He did not originally belong to Liangshan. He was a deputy under Zhang Qing, the Featherless Arrow, commander of Dongchang. Zhang Qing could hit men with thrown stones with unfailing accuracy, injuring more than a dozen Liangshan heroes in succession and building an imposing reputation. Ding Desun and Gong Wang, the Flower-necked Tiger, were his trusted right and left hands in defending the prefecture. Gong Wang had tiger stripes tattooed over his body and a tiger's head around his neck, and excelled at throwing spears. Ding Desun used a flying fork, handling it expertly on horseback or on foot and hurling it to wound opponents. Like Gong Wang, he was an experienced and formidable fighter under Zhang Qing.

After taking Dongping and capturing Dong Ping, the General of Two Spears, Song Jiang marched against Dongchang, seeking achievements separately from Lu Junyi. The armies faced each other beneath the city. Zhang Qing drove his troops forward and sent stones flying like rain, repeatedly wounding Liangshan's commanders and checking their momentum. Ding Desun and Gong Wang rode out to assist, each displaying his skill and courage. Yet destiny favored Liangshan's rise. Following Wu Yong's plan, Song Jiang laid an ambush, drew Zhang Qing too far forward and trapped the Featherless Arrow and his horse in a bog, capturing him alive for the mountain. Gong Wang was also taken, and Ding Desun was seized amid the confused fighting. When the three were brought before the Hall of Loyalty and Righteousness, Song Jiang personally untied them, treated them with courtesy and offered kind reassurance. Moved by his righteousness, Zhang Qing agreed to submit. His two faithful deputies followed their commander, bowed to the ground and sincerely pledged to join the brotherhood. Ding Desun thus entered Liangshan and became one of the 108.

At Liangshan's great assembly, when the Heavenly and Earthly Stars' places were fixed, Ding Desun received the Earthly Speed Star and the seventy-ninth seat. He served as an infantry officer alongside Gong Wang and other surrendered commanders, ready for deployment at the front. Although not highly ranked, his throwing-fork skill and readiness to die made him useful in charges and assaults against strong defenses. Whenever the army moved, he fought with its mounted and foot formations and never shirked his work.

After the whole band accepted the imperial amnesty, Ding Desun followed the court's campaigns against Great Liao, Tian Hu in Hebei and Wang Qing in Huaixi. He risked his life and repeatedly earned modest distinction. His doom came in the southern campaign against Fang La, a savage war that cost many chieftains. The army advanced into central Zhejiang and fought among mountain valleys and perilous passes. Jiangnan's tangled terrain and thick vegetation sheltered poisonous snakes and dangerous insects. While crossing a mountain ridge on the march, Ding Desun was unexpectedly bitten on the foot by a venomous snake. The poison reached his heart before treatment could save him, and he died. This valiant man had followed Zhang Qing and campaigned north and south, surviving clashes between armies and all their swords, spears, arrows and stones, only to die of a snake's venom deep in the mountains. His end was bitterly undeserved. After Song Jiang returned and reported the army's merits, the fallen received posthumous honors. Ding Desun, who had campaigned in righteousness and died in imperial service, was granted the title Gentleman of Righteous Integrity in recognition of his loyalty.

A surrendered officer at first, Ding Desun adhered to righteousness once he joined Liangshan. He did not dwell on distinctions between former and new masters, but devoted himself to faithful service. His name was not especially prominent, yet his flying fork and courage made him a worthy officer among the Earthly Fiends. Death by snakebite was no failure in battle; it was the turn of fate. Readers reaching this point may well sigh for the Arrow-struck Tiger: a veteran of a hundred fights escaped arrows and stones only to be killed by an obscure little creature. Such is the unpredictability of the world.
丁得孙者，泰州人氏，本东昌府守将之裨将也。生得面颊及项，遍长疤痕，盖少时屡经矢石.ja:
丁得孫は泰州の出身で、もとは東昌府を守る将の副将だった。頬や首には一面に傷痕があり、若いころから矢石の中をくぐって重ねた古傷だったため、江湖では「中箭虎」と呼ばれた。この名には二つの意味がある。矢傷が虎の縞のようにまだらであることと、性格が猛虎に似て、戦場で刃や矢を避けず、流れ矢を受けても退かぬことである。見る者は、縦横に傷の走る恐ろしい顔から、身を迫る殺伐の気を感じた。

丁得孫は初めから梁山の者ではなく、東昌府の守将、没羽箭・張清の配下だった。張清は石を投げて人を打つことに巧みで、百発百中の腕により梁山の好漢十数人を続けて負傷させ、大いに威勢を上げていた。丁得孫と花項虎・龔旺はその左右の腕として東昌を守った。龔旺は全身に虎の縞、首に虎の頭を彫り、飛槍を得意とした。一方の丁得孫は飛叉を使い、馬上でも徒歩でも巧みに扱い、投げて相手を傷つけることもできた。どちらも張清の幕下にあって、戦に慣れた猛将だった。

宋公明は東平府を破って双槍将・董平を捕らえた後、盧俊義と分かれて功を争うべく、兵を率いて東昌府へ来た。城下で向かい合うと、張清は兵馬を進め、雨のように飛石を放った。梁山の諸将は次々と傷つき、勢いをくじかれた。丁得孫と龔旺も、それぞれの技を頼みに馬を出し、先頭で勇を振るった。だが天命は梁山の隆盛を定めていた。宋江は呉用の策で伏兵を置き、張清を深く誘い込み、人馬もろとも泥沼へ陥れて生け捕りにした。龔旺も捕らえられ、丁得孫も乱軍の中で梁山の好漢に取り押さえられた。三将が忠義堂の前へ連れて来られると、宋江は自ら縄を解き、礼を尽くし、優しい言葉で慰めた。張清は義気に感じて帰順を願い、長く従ってきた龔旺と丁得孫も、主将が降ったのを見て心を定め、地に伏して、ともに山へ入り大義に集うことを誓った。こうして丁得孫も百八人に加わった。

梁山の大聚義で天罡地煞の席次が定められると、丁得孫は地速星に応じる第七十九位に座った。歩軍将校として龔旺ら降将と並び、陣前で命令を待つ役目だった。上位ではないものの、飛叉の技と死を恐れぬ勇気は、敵陣への突撃や堅い守りの突破に役立った。軍が動くたびに歩騎の隊列に交じって戦い、怠けることはなかった。

宋公明ら全員が招安を受けると、朝廷の命で大遼、河北の田虎、淮西の王慶を討った。丁得孫も従軍し、生死の間を出入りして、たびたび小さな功を立てた。多くの頭領を失う方臘征討の江南では、彼にも最期が訪れた。軍が浙江中部へ進み、険しい谷や関を転戦していたころである。江南は地形が複雑で草木も深く、毒蛇や害虫が潜んでいた。山道を行く丁得孫は、思いがけず毒蛇に足を噛まれ、毒が心臓へ回り、治療が間に合わず死んでしまった。張清に従い南北を転戦し、刀槍や矢石の下にも死ななかった好漢が、深山の一匹の蛇に命を奪われたとは、無念なことである。宋江が凱旋して功績を奏上すると、戦死した将には追封が行われた。義に従って征き、王事に死んだ丁得孫もその列に入り、忠義をたたえて義節郎を贈られた。

丁得孫はもと降将だったが、梁山へ入ってからは「義」の一字を守り、旧主と新主の違いにこだわらず、ただ忠を尽くした。名は目立たなくとも、飛叉の技と陣前の勇気によって、地煞の中で十分に働ける将だった。蛇に噛まれて死んだのは戦の落ち度でなく、天数のなせる業である。百戦を経て矢石にも倒れぬ者が、名もない小さな生き物に命を落とす。世の無常はおおむねこのようなものだと、読者も中箭虎のために深く嘆息せずにはいられない。

董平者，河东上党郡人氏，原是东平府兵马都监。其人英武绝伦，仪表非凡，惯使两条钢枪.en:
Dong Ping came from Shangdang Commandery in Hedong and originally served as military superintendent of Dongping Prefecture. Exceptionally valiant and striking in appearance, he wielded two steel spears, striking on either side and ranging freely through battle with a force that ten thousand men could not withstand. Hence his nickname, the General of Two Spears. Beyond his martial excellence, he was graceful and cultivated, understood many musical instruments and could write and paint. His command of both civil and military accomplishments also earned him praise as the Elegant General of Two Spears. His Dongping banner often bore the couplet “Heroic general of twin spears; elegant lord of ten thousand households,” expressing his pride in his talents and looks and his disdain for rivals.

He joined Liangshan through Song Jiang's campaign against Dongping. Liangshan's army was strong and sought the money and provisions of Dongping and Dongchang for military use. Song Jiang and Lu Junyi each led an army toward one city, while Wu Yong coordinated their movements. They agreed that whoever captured his city first would take precedence, settling the question of Liangshan's chief leadership. Song Jiang first sent Yu Baosi and Wang Dingliu into Dongping with a letter, but Prefect Cheng Wanli arrested them, jailed them and nearly had them beheaded, making the two sides bitter enemies. As military superintendent, Dong Ping rode out on the prefect's orders to fight Liangshan. His horse and spears ranged back and forth, the two steel weapons spinning in an impenetrable storm. Several Liangshan officers fought him in succession without defeating him. Watching this formidable display, Song Jiang secretly applauded his ability and resolved to win such a man. He repeatedly consulted Wu Yong on schemes to bring Dong Ping over, unwilling to destroy a worthy hero by force of arms.

Brave though he was, Dong Ping nursed a grievance. He had long admired Cheng Wanli's daughter and repeatedly sought her hand, but the prefect disdained his soldier's background and refused, leaving him resentful. Song Jiang learned of this and used it. Han Tao, Xu Ning and others set an ambush and lured him forward while words were used to stir his feelings. Captured in Liangshan's trap, Dong Ping was personally untied by Song Jiang and courteously treated. Song repeatedly urged him to surrender and promised to take Dongping and bring about his desired marriage. Already bitter toward Cheng and moved by Song's apparent sincerity, Dong Ping agreed. He immediately turned against his former master, tricked the guards into opening the gate and led Liangshan's troops into Dongping. He personally killed the prefect's family, seized Miss Cheng and helped take the city's money and grain. Dongping fell, and he formally joined Liangshan.

Not long after his arrival, the great assembly brought all 108 heroes together in the Hall of Loyalty and Righteousness to settle their ranks. Although a recent recruit, Dong Ping's exceptional martial skill and conspicuous service earned him a place among the Heavenly Spirits. Ranked fifteenth as the Heavenly Standing Star, he shared cavalry responsibilities with Zhang Qing, Xu Ning and others, serving as a valiant cavalry commander outside the Five Tiger Generals. Throughout Liangshan's wars he often led the vanguard, charging into hostile formations with both spears circling to either side. Almost irresistible in his advances, he was a rare and valuable warrior among the cavalry.

After the amnesty Dong Ping campaigned north and south with Song Jiang, serving against Liao and Fang La and repeatedly earning distinction. Yet fate gave his talent a terrible end. When the army attacked Dusong Pass in the Fang La campaign, its defenders Li Tianrun, Zhang Tao and others proved exceptionally hard to overcome. Dong Ping's left arm was struck and injured by a cannon stone. Though unfit for combat, he was eager to earn merit and avenge lost brothers. He bound the wounded arm, forced himself to take up his spear and went with Zhang Qing to challenge the enemy below the pass. Li Tianrun and Zhang Tao came out to fight. Unable to use both spears with his injured arm, Dong Ping struggled to defend himself. In the melee Zhang Tao cut him in two at the waist. The extraordinary General of Two Spears died beneath Dusong Pass on the same day as his friend Zhang Qing. Elegant, dashing and accomplished in letters and arms, he had been one of Liangshan's finest men. Instead of a peaceful ending, he received a warrior's shroud, leaving only the fame of his heroic twin spears to later generations.
董平者，河东上党郡人氏，原是东平府兵马都监。其人英武绝伦，仪表非凡，惯使两条钢枪.ja:
董平は河東上党郡の出身で、もとは東平府の兵馬都監だった。武勇に秀で、容姿も非凡で、二本の鋼槍を左右に操って戦場を縦横に駆け、万夫も防げぬほどだったため、「双槍将」と呼ばれた。武芸だけでなく風雅な教養もあり、さまざまな楽器に通じ、書画もよくする文武両道の人物で、「風流双槍将」の美称も持った。東平府の旗にはしばしば「英雄双槍将、風流万戸侯」と記され、それは自らの才貌を誇り、当代を睥睨する姿の表れだった。

董平が梁山へ入ったのは、宋江の東平府攻略が縁である。当時、梁山泊は兵馬が充実し、軍用の金糧を得ようと東平、東昌の二府を狙った。宋江と盧俊義が一軍ずつ率い、呉用が調整し、先に城を落とした者を上位とする約束で、梁山の首領の序列を決めようとした。宋江はまず郁保四と王定六を入城させて書状を届けたが、太守の程万里は二人を捕らえて牢へ入れ、危うく斬首するところだった。こうして両軍は深い敵となった。兵馬都監の董平は太守の命で出陣し、梁山の諸将と戦った。馬を走らせ槍を構え、二本の鋼槍を風雨も通さぬほどに使い、幾人もの将と続けて戦っても、誰も勝てなかった。その威風を見た宋江は心中で喝采し、惜しい人才だと思って呉用と何度も策を練った。刀兵でこの好漢を失わせず、何としても梁山へ迎えたかったのである。

勇猛な董平にも、心のわだかまりがあった。東平太守・程万里の娘を長く慕い、幾度も縁組を求めたが、太守は武人の出であることを嫌って許さず、董平は恨みを抱いていた。事情を知った宋江は、これを利用した。韓滔や徐寧らに伏兵を設けて誘わせる一方、言葉でも心を揺さぶった。計略に落ちた董平を宋江は自ら縄を解いて礼遇し、東平を破って望む縁組をかなえると約束して、繰り返し帰順を勧めた。太守への積年の恨みと、宋江の誠意に動かされた董平は降伏を決めた。そしてすぐに矛を返し、城門を欺いて開かせ、梁山軍を東平府へ導いた。自ら程太守一家を殺し、娘を奪い、城の金糧を得た。こうして東平府は落ち、董平は正式に梁山の仲間となった。

入山して間もなく大聚義が行われ、百八人が忠義堂に集まって席次を定めた。董平は後から帰順した者ながら、抜群の武芸と戦功により天罡に入り、第十五位の天立星となった。張清、徐寧らと馬軍を担い、五虎将以外の馬軍驍将を務めた。梁山のさまざまな戦では、しばしば先鋒となって敵陣へ突入し、二本の鋼槍を左右に巡らせ、行く先々を打ち破った。馬軍にとって得難い猛将だった。

招安後、董平は宋江に従って南北を転戦し、遼や方臘との戦いで陣前に尽くし、たびたび功を立てた。しかし天は英才を妬んだのか、その最期は惨烈だった。方臘征討で独松関を攻めたとき、守将の厲天閏や張韜らは勇猛で、容易には破れなかった。ある日、董平は砲石を受けて左腕を負傷した。本来は出陣すべきでなかったが、功を急ぎ、失われた兄弟の仇を討とうとして、傷ついた腕を縛り、無理に槍を取って張清と関の下へ戦を求めに行った。厲天閏と張韜が出てくると、左腕の傷で双槍を使えず、防ぐのも難しかった。乱戦の中、張韜の一刀が董平を腰から両断した。比類なき双槍将は独松関の下で、親友の張清と同じ日に戦死したのである。風流で颯爽とし、文武を兼ねた梁山屈指の人物も、馬革に屍を包まれ、安らかな最期は得られなかった。「英雄双槍」の名だけが後世へ伝わったのは、まことに嘆かわしい。
