From noble military descent and command at Runing to Liangshan's Five Tigers and final defense of the state, his loyalty and courage never changed. He upheld the Huyan family's fame and fulfilled his lifelong heroic purpose in acting for Heaven and serving his country.
呼延灼，乃开国名将河东名将呼延赞之嫡派子孙，世受国恩，原是汝宁郡都统制，统领一郡.ja:
呼延灼は、開国の名将、河東の呼延賛の直系の子孫である。代々国恩を受け、もとは汝寧郡都統制として一郡の軍馬を率いていた。堂々たる姿で、水磨きの八角鋼鞭を二本使い、左は十二斤、右は十三斤あった。戦場で左右に巡らせれば疾風驟雨のようで、誰も近寄れなかったため、「双鞭呼延灼」と呼ばれた。愛馬は「踢雪烏騅」といい、全身漆黒で四蹄だけ雪のように白く、一日に千里を走る名馬だった。双鞭と相まって、八方を威圧する姿であった。

宋江らが官府を襲い州県を騒がせ、梁山の名が高まると、朝廷は驚いた。高太尉の推挙によって呼延灼が兵馬指揮使となり、大軍で水泊を討つことになった。彼は陳州団練使の百勝将・韓滔と、潁州団練使の天目将・彭玘を副将に推し、三路の兵を率いて進んだ。陣前で用いた家伝の切り札は連環馬である。三千の鉄騎を三十頭ずつつなぎ、人馬とも鎧を着け、長槍や大戟を壁のように進めた。矢も刀槍も通らず、突撃と包囲で梁山を何度も敗り、多くを失わせた。ようやく金銭豹子・湯隆が、鉤鎌槍の製作と使用に通じる従兄、金槍手・徐寧の招致を献策した。呉用が計略で山へ迎え、徐寧が歩兵に槍法を教えると、再来した連環馬の脚を狙い、馬は乱れて互いを踏んだ。呼延灼は大敗し、全軍が散り散りとなった。

独り逃れた彼は都へ戻る顔がなく、青州の慕容知府を頼り、桃花山、二竜山、白虎山を攻めるよう命じられた。三山の好漢は支えきれず、苦戦しながら梁山へ援助を求めた。宋江は自ら大軍を率いて来て、幾度か将が戦った末、呉用の策で呼延灼を落とし穴へ誘い、生け捕りにした。宋江は自ら縄を解き、頭を下げ、忠義と人才を迎える志、替天行道の意味を詳しく説いた。呼延灼は家族への懸念もなくなり、深い義気にも感じて、感服して帰順した。さらに巧計で青州の門を開かせ、慕容知府を生け捕りにして、先の使役への恨みを晴らし、大功を立てた。

大聚義では天罡の第八位、天威星となり、関勝、林冲、秦明、董平と並ぶ馬軍五虎将の一人となった。大戦のたび双鞭を持って出馬し、敵将と数十合を交えても勝負がつかぬほどで、山寨が長城のように頼る上将だった。武芸の高さと戦場での落ち着きは、五虎の中でも優れていた。

招安後は宋江と遼、田虎、王慶、方臘を討ち、鞍馬の苦労の中で戦功を重ね、双鞭の下で無数の将を敗った。多くの英雄が散る中でも身を保ち、方臘平定後に生還した。朝廷は御営兵馬指揮使に任じ、都で命を待たせ、彼は再び官軍の軍装を着た。後に金軍が大挙して南侵すると、老将として鎧を着け、軍を率いて外敵を防ぎ、各地を転戦した。最後は淮西で力戦して死に、王事に命を捧げた。名門の後裔、汝寧の都統から、水泊の五虎、国を守って死ぬ将へと歩んだ一生は、忠勇において変わらなかった。呼延家代々の将門の名を辱めず、天に代わって道を行い、国に尽くし、仁を求めて仁を得て、英雄の志を全うしたのである。

花荣，清风寨知寨，乃将门之子，世代簪缨，原做青州清风寨副知寨，掌一寨军马。其人年.en:
Hua Rong served as deputy commander of Qingfeng Fort in Qingzhou, coming from a hereditary military family. Young, handsome and refined, with red lips, white teeth and delicate features, he wielded a long spear and possessed miraculous archery. He could pierce a willow leaf at a hundred paces and never wasted a shot. People compared him to the Han flying general Li Guang and called him Little Li Guang Hua Rong. Drawing his bow like a full moon and sending arrows like shooting stars, he was the novel's foremost kind of master archer.

An old acquaintance of Song Jiang, he corresponded regularly with him and admired his character. After killing Yan Poxi and being exiled to Jiangzhou, Song Jiang passed Qingfeng Mountain, where Yan Shun and Wang Ying nearly mistook him for a merchant to be killed for his heart. Naming himself instead made him an honored guest. He then visited Hua Rong at Qingfeng Fort. During the Lantern Festival, the wife of chief commander Liu Gao, whom Song Jiang had previously rescued on the mountain, repaid him with betrayal and accused him of being a bandit. Liu Gao imprisoned him. Furious, Hua Rong led men to forcibly recover Song Jiang, and fighting broke out. Liu Gao appealed to Qingzhou, whose prefect sent Qin Ming, the Thunderbolt, with an army. When government soldiers dismissed Hua Rong's reputation, he shot a cord on the fort gate and then severed an enemy officer's helmet tassel, terrifying them with his accuracy. Qin Ming was later captured by a ruse, and Song Jiang contrived to make him an outlaw, also marrying Hua Rong's sister to him. Hua Rong, Qin Ming, Yan Shun, Huang Xin and the Qingfeng forces all went to Liangshan.

His archery became one of Liangshan's sharpest unconventional weapons. Later, when Song Jiang occupied the second seat and sought amnesty, imperial messengers brought a proclamation whose contemptuous language, coupled with their withholding imperial wine, angered the heroes. Li Kui tore the decree and cursed the envoy in the hall, causing turmoil. Hua Rong also demonstrated his skill before the troops: when a flock of geese passed overhead, one arrow brought down the leader instantly. The entire camp was awed. This episode around the heroes' ranking particularly displays the divine accuracy with which he outshone the army.

At the great assembly Hua Rong ranked ninth among the Heavenly Spirits as the Heavenly Hero Star. He became one of the Eight Valiant Cavalry and Vanguard Commissioners, sharing advance duties with men such as Lin Chong, Qin Ming, Huyan Zhuo and Dong Ping. Whether besieging cities, fighting in the open or defeating enemies at range, his arrows served at the front and won merit. He was a pillar of the stronghold and one of Song Jiang's closest, most trusted and capable brothers.

After the amnesty he campaigned against Liao, Tian Hu, Wang Qing and Fang La, shooting unerringly and winning illustrious honors while surviving the battles. After Fang La's defeat he was appointed military commander of Yingtian Prefecture and might have enjoyed wealth and a peaceful old age. Instead Gao Qiu, Yang Jian and other corrupt ministers secretly poisoned Song Jiang and Lu Junyi, who died one after the other. Hua Rong and Wu Yong were devastated. Remembering a lifetime of brotherhood and lamenting that loyal men could not survive under wicked ministers, they traveled together to Song Jiang's grave in Chuzhou. Weeping before it, they concluded that even continued life would leave them vulnerable to those ministers and chose death to fulfill their bond. Beside Song Jiang's tomb at Liao'er Marsh, both hanged themselves from trees, following their elder brother below the earth. The court later granted them posthumous rank. The elegant Little Li Guang, a celebrated archer, had risen from deputy fort commander to Liangshan cavalry vanguard and finally died for his loyalty at a grave. His shooting and devoted friendship make his story one of Water Margin's most sorrowful.
花荣，清风寨知寨，乃将门之子，世代簪缨，原做青州清风寨副知寨，掌一寨军马。其人年.ja:
花栄は将門の子で、代々官に仕えた家に生まれ、青州清風寨の副知寨として軍馬を掌握していた。若く、赤い唇と白い歯、端正な目鼻立ち、すらりとした非凡な姿を持ち、長槍と神業の弓を使った。百歩の先の柳葉を射抜き、一矢も外さぬため、漢の飛将・李広にたとえられ、「小李広花栄」と呼ばれた。満月のように弓を引き、流星のように矢を放つ、作中でも第一級の神射手である。

宋江とは旧知で、常に書状を交わして人柄を慕っていた。閻婆惜を殺して江州へ流された宋江が清風山を通ると、燕順や王英らに商人と誤認され、腹を裂いて心臓を取られかけた。名を告げたことで逆に上客となり、その後、花栄を頼って清風寨へ来た。元宵の灯見物の際、正知寨・劉高の妻は、以前清風山で宋江に救われたにもかかわらず、恩を仇で返して山賊だと訴えた。投獄を聞いた花栄は激怒し、兵を率いて宋江を強引に奪い返した。戦となり、劉高の急報で慕容知府が霹靂火・秦明を大軍とともに送った。官軍が花栄を名ばかりと見くびると、彼は一矢で寨門の房紐を射、次には敵将の兜の房を射切って、正確さに震え上がらせた。後に秦明が計略で捕らえられると、宋江は彼を山賊に引き込み、花栄の妹を妻とした。花栄、秦明、燕順、黄信ら清風山と清風寨の人馬は、皆梁山へ向かった。

入山後、神射は梁山の大戦で最も鋭い奇兵の一つとなった。後に第二席となった宋江が招安を求めると、朝廷の使者が持参した詔書の軽侮する文言と、御酒の横領が好漢を怒らせた。李逵が堂で詔書を破り使者を罵って大騒ぎになる中、花栄も兵の前で技を見せた。空を過ぎる雁の群れに弓を引き、一矢で先頭の雁を射落としたのである。全軍が驚き服したこの席次決定前後の一幕は、軍を圧する神業の弓をよく示している。

大聚義では天罡の第九位、天英星となり、馬軍八驃騎兼先鋒使の一人に任じられた。林冲、秦明、呼延灼、董平らと先鋒を担い、攻城でも野戦でも遠射で敵を破るときでも、常に前で功を立てた。山寨の柱であり、宋江に最も信頼される、有能で親密な兄弟の一人だった。

招安後は遼、田虎、王慶、方臘を討ち、馬を駆けて一矢も外さず、赫々たる功を立てて生き残った。凱旋すると応天府都統制を授かり、富貴を享受して余生を送ることもできた。ところが高俅、楊戩ら奸臣が宋江と盧俊義を毒酒や毒物で害し、二人は相次いで死んだ。花栄と呉用は深く悲しみ、一生の兄弟の義を思い、奸佞の世では忠良が生きられぬと嘆いて、ともに楚州の宋江の墓へ赴いた。墓前で慟哭し、生き続けても奸臣に狙われるなら死んで義を全うしようと考え、蓼児窪の墓のそばの木で、ともに首をくくり、地下の兄に従った。後に朝廷は爵を追封した。風雅な神射の名将は、副知寨から水泊の先鋒へ進み、最後には墓前で義に殉じた。その弓と情義は、ともに『水滸伝』で最も嘆きを誘う物語の一つとして伝わる。

镇三山黄信，青州人氏，原是青州指挥司统制慕容知府帐下的兵马都监，乃梁山泊七十二地.en:
Huang Xin, the Subduer of Three Mountains, came from Qingzhou and originally served as military superintendent under its command headquarters and Prefect Murong. One of the seventy-two Earthly Fiends, he corresponded to the Earthly Fiend Star, ranked thirty-eighth and served as a junior cavalry commander and long-range scouting chief. He used a death-dealing sword, was skilled and fierce, and spoke with great confidence. Qingzhou had three outlaw mountains, Qingfeng, Twin Dragons and Peach Blossom. Claiming that his own ability could clear all three and destroy their bands, he styled himself the Subduer of Three Mountains. The name conveyed official arrogance and youthful zeal, while preparing the irony of his later humiliation.

He was Qin Ming's pupil. The Thunderbolt commanded Qingzhou's forces, wielded a wolf-toothed mace and had a fiery temper. Huang Xin learned fine martial skills from him and gained a local reputation. At Qingfeng Fort, deputy commander Hua Rong was at odds with chief Liu Gao. Liu's wife, rescued by Song Jiang after being captured on the mountain, repaid him by accusing him of being the bandit chief and helping frame Hua Rong. Prefect Murong sent Huang Xin to arrest them. Putting on an imposing show, he arranged a feast, lured Hua Rong into attending and ordered his men to seize him. He and Song Jiang were locked in prison carts for delivery to Qingzhou. But beneath Qingfeng Mountain, Yan Shun, Wang Ying and Zheng Tianshou intercepted them. Huang Xin tried to demonstrate his vaunted prowess, but was outnumbered and ambushed. Nearly killed, he abandoned the carts and rode back to Qingzhou. Far from subduing the mountains, he had been routed by their men, turning his nickname into a joke.

Enraged at his return, Prefect Murong sent Qin Ming with an army against Qingfeng Mountain. But Hua Rong and Song Jiang's schemes brought Qin Ming's defeat, deception at the city and his family's murder by the prefect. With nowhere to turn, he became an outlaw himself. He then personally called Huang Xin from below the city. Moved by their teacher-pupil bond and seeing that resistance was hopeless, Huang Xin opened the gate and surrendered, joining the band with his master and later going to Liangshan. He thereafter served as a cavalry leader available for campaign orders.

At the assembly he received the thirty-eighth seat among the Earthly Fiends and served in the cavalry with Qin Ming. His work chiefly involved distant scouting and battlefield assaults as a subordinate officer. He was not a leading figure like the Five Tigers or Eight Valiant Cavalry, but was diligent and devoted. In the two defeats of Tong Guan and three of Gao Qiu he fought with the army and did not disgrace his name.

After the amnesty Huang Xin served Song Jiang against Liao and Fang La, contributing greatly from the saddle. Remarkably, though more than half the 108 were lost in Jiangnan, seven of ten gone and many returning only in shrouds, he survived among the fortunate few. After Fang La's defeat and the return, he was granted the rank Gentleman of Martial Grace and command over forces on the various routes, returning to Qingzhou for official employment. An officer restored from outlawry, he had started as Qingzhou's military superintendent, made a long circuit through life and finally grew old in office in the same place. It was one of the book's rare peaceful conclusions.
镇三山黄信，青州人氏，原是青州指挥司统制慕容知府帐下的兵马都监，乃梁山泊七十二地.ja:
鎮三山・黄信は青州の出身で、もとは青州指揮司と慕容知府のもとで兵馬都監を務めた。七十二地煞の地煞星に応じる第三十八位、馬軍小彪将兼遠探出哨頭領である。喪門剣を使い、武芸に優れ、気性は激しく、口も大きかった。青州の清風山、二竜山、桃花山には賊が拠り、黄信は自分一人の技で三山を平らげ、群盗を一掃すると豪語した。そのため自他ともに鎮三山と呼んだのである。官の威勢と若い鋭気に満ちる名は、後のつまずきの伏線にもなった。

黄信は霹靂火・秦明の弟子だった。秦明は青州の軍馬を統べ、狼牙棒を使い、烈火のような性を持った。黄信は師から優れた武芸を学び、一帯で名を上げた。当時清風寨の副知寨・花栄は正知寨・劉高と不仲だった。劉高の妻は清風山にさらわれ、宋江に救われながら、恩を仇で返して彼を賊首と訴え、花栄も陥れた。慕容知府は黄信を逮捕に送り、黄信は威勢を張って宴席を設け、花栄を誘い出して捕らえた。宋江とともに囚人車へ閉じ込め、青州へ送って功を求めようとしたが、清風山の下で錦毛虎・燕順、矮脚虎・王英、白面郎君・鄭天寿に遮られた。鎮三山の力を見せようにも、多勢と伏兵に抗せず、危うく命を落としかけ、車を捨てて逃げ帰った。三山を鎮めるどころか山の者に敗走させられ、その名は笑い話となった。

慕容知府は怒り、師の秦明を大軍とともに送った。しかし秦明も花栄と宋江の策に陥り、城で欺かれ、家族を知府に殺され、行き場をなくして山賊となった。帰順した秦明が自ら城下から弟子を呼ぶと、黄信は師弟の情と大勢の去ったことを思い、門を開いて降った。師と同じ一団へ加わり、後に梁山の大寨へ上った。以後は馬軍頭領として征討の命に従った。

大聚義では地煞の第三十八位に座り、秦明と同じ馬軍に列した。主な役割は遠方の偵察や敵陣への突入を行う副将で、五虎や八驃のような頂点の人物ではないが、勤勉に命を尽くす戦将だった。童貫を二度、高俅を三度破る大戦でも随軍して戦い、名を辱めなかった。

招安後は宋江と遼、方臘を討ち、鞍馬の間で大いに働いた。江南では百八人の半数以上、十のうち七が失われ、多くの兄弟が馬革に包まれて生還できなかったが、黄信は無事に戻れた数少ない一人だった。方臘平定後、武奕郎と諸路都統領を授かり、再び青州で任用され、故郷の朝廷の官となった。青州の兵馬都監から山賊を経て官へ戻り、大きく巡った末に同じ青州で官として老いた。これも本書では稀な安らかな結末である。

皇甫端，绰号「紫髯伯」，幽州人氏。此人生得碧眼黄须，形貌奇异，宛若胡人，颔下一部.en:
Huangfu Duan, the Purple-bearded Elder, came from Youzhou. With blue-green eyes, yellow whiskers and an unusual appearance resembling a foreigner, he wore a long purple beard flowing across his chest and possessed a distinguished bearing. His beard recalled Sun Quan of Eastern Wu in the Three Kingdoms, who had blue-green eyes and a purple beard and was called the Purple-bearded Youth. Huangfu Duan's own nickname also acknowledged his expertise in treating and judging horses, abilities comparable to the legendary horse connoisseur Bole.

Though counted among Liangshan's heroes, he was not an assault commander but an excellent veterinarian. Particularly skilled with horses, he could treat illness, coughing, wasting, injuries and epidemics. By observing their condition and bearing, then applying acupuncture, cautery and medicines, he cured their ailments. He could also distinguish fine horses from inferior ones, understand their temperaments and judge their endurance. The north had produced famous horses since the Three Kingdoms, and the people of You and Yan were accustomed to riding and archery. Growing up in Youzhou, Huangfu Duan learned veterinary medicine from childhood and became renowned for his extraordinary skill. He later practiced in Dongchang, running a shop that treated cattle, horses and other livestock, with a reputation throughout Hebei.

His entry into Liangshan followed the surrender of Zhang Qing, the Featherless Arrow. During the attacks on Dongping and Dongchang, the latter was defended by Zhang Qing, whose unerring thrown stones struck fifteen Liangshan chieftains and initially prevented victory. Song Jiang and Wu Yong eventually lured him into a trap and captured him. Admiring his skill, Song Jiang personally untied him and treated him courteously, winning his submission. Zhang Qing then recommended two old acquaintances: a physician of veterinary background who could treat people, and Huangfu Duan, who treated animals. An old Dongchang friend, Huangfu Duan was recommended because Zhang Qing knew how useful his skill would be to the army. Song Jiang welcomed his imposing presence and rare expertise with horses. With so many men and countless mounts, Liangshan greatly benefited from a master veterinarian in maintaining its animals and preparing for war.

At the assembly Huangfu Duan received the Earthly Beast Star and the fifty-seventh seat among the Earthly Fiends. He supervised horse management and veterinary care as the army's chief veterinarian. His duties involved no killing, yet warhorses were essential: cavalry charges depended on good mounts. By keeping them well fed, strong and less vulnerable to illness and loss, he made an important contribution. The Earthly Beast Star precisely suited his knowledge of animals and horses.

After the amnesty he followed the army against Great Liao, Tian Hu, Wang Qing and Fang La. Whenever its horses were injured or sick, his care kept the cavalry from losing effectiveness. His labor was arduous and valuable, but he was no frontline fighter and took no part in close combat, allowing him to survive the major battles. In the Fang La campaign seven or eight of every ten Liangshan heroes were lost, yet his specialist, noncombatant duties allowed him to return unharmed.

After the victory and return to court, the surviving leaders received rewards. Valuing Huangfu Duan's veterinary skill, the emperor retained him in the capital as chief commissioner of the Imperial Horse Directorate, responsible for the royal stables and the sovereign's mounts. His specialist craft thus secured both his livelihood and a peaceful end in the capital, where he enjoyed his official salary. Unlike so many brothers, he did not return in a shroud or perish abroad, becoming one of the fortunate Earthly Fiends who preserved their lives and enjoyed a good outcome.

Huangfu Duan began as a horse doctor and entered the company of 108 through Zhang Qing's recommendation. Neither renowned for military victories nor distinguished in martial arts, he was valued by Song Jiang for his exceptional skill in judging horses and treating animals. That same skill won him imperial favor and a capital appointment, giving his story a fortunate beginning and ending. With purple beard, blue-green eyes and Bole-like knowledge, he is a distinctive figure among Water Margin's heroes.
皇甫端，绰号「紫髯伯」，幽州人氏。此人生得碧眼黄须，形貌奇异，宛若胡人，颔下一部.ja:
皇甫端は、あだ名を「紫髯伯」といい、幽州の出身である。碧眼に黄色い髭という異様な姿で胡人に似ており、顎から胸へ長い紫の髭を垂らす威儀があったため、この名で呼ばれた。三国時代の呉の孫権も碧眼紫髯で紫髯児といわれたが、皇甫端の髭の色はそれに似ていた。さらに馬の治療に通じることから、伯楽のように馬を見分け、治せるという意味も込められていた。

梁山に名を連ねても、皇甫端は突撃の将ではなく、優れた獣医だった。特に馬の病、咳や喘ぎ、衰弱、転倒の傷、疫病を得意とし、気配と形を見て、鍼、焼灼、薬で治した。良馬と駄馬を見分け、性質や脚力も知っていた。北地は三国のころから名馬を産し、幽燕の人は騎射に慣れていた。幽州に育った彼も幼くして獣医の術を学び、絶妙な腕で遠近に知られた。後には東昌府で店を開き、牛馬などの家畜を専門に診て、河北に名を広めた。

入山は没羽箭・張清の帰順が縁だった。梁山が東平、東昌を攻めた際、東昌を守る張清は飛石百発百中の技で十五人の頭領を打ち、容易に勝たせなかった。後に宋江と呉用が計略で伏兵へ誘い、生け捕りにした。武芸を慕う宋江が自ら縄を解いて礼遇すると、張清は恩義に感じて帰順した。その際、獣医の出で人を診る医士と、動物を診る紫髯伯・皇甫端という二人の旧知を推挙した。東昌で親しかった張清は、皇甫端の技が軍に大いに役立つと知っていたのである。堂々たる姿と相馬、医馬の奇術を見た宋江は、軍に必要な人才だと喜んで迎えた。人馬の多い梁山に神業の獣医が加わることは、馬の飼育と戦の準備に大きな利益だった。

大聚義では地煞の地獣星、第五十七位となり、馬の管理と獣医の事を統べる総管になった。殺伐の役ではなくとも、騎兵の突撃は良馬にかかっている。治療と調養で三軍の乗馬を太らせて丈夫にし、病や損失を減らした功は忘れられない。地獣星の号も、その専門にまさしくふさわしかった。

招安後は大遼、田虎、王慶、方臘の征討に従った。軍馬が傷つき病むたびに世話と治療をし、騎兵が馬の病で戦力を失わぬよう支えた。苦労も功も大きかったが、戦闘の将ではなく斬り合いに加わらないため、各大戦を無事に越えた。方臘征討では好漢の十に七、八が失われたものの、専門の獣医として前線に立たず、身を全うして帰った。

方臘平定後、朝廷が生存者の功を賞すると、皇甫端の技術を惜しんで都に留め、御馬監大使に封じた。皇家の厩の馬を管理し、天子の乗馬を治す役である。これにより一芸で身を立て、朝廷の俸禄を受け、都で安らかに生涯を終えた。多くの兄弟のように馬革に包まれたり、異郷で散ったりせず、命を保って善果を得た地煞の稀な一人だった。

皇甫端は馬を診る獣医から、張清の推薦で百八人に入った。赫々たる戦功や武芸はなくとも、相馬と医獣の絶技によって宋江に重んじられ、最後には同じ技で朝廷の寵を得て都の官となり、始終を全うした。紫髯碧眼に伯楽の力を備える、『水滸伝』の群英の中でも独特の人物である。

蒋敬，绰号「神算子」，乃梁山泊一百单八将中地会星，居地煞之列，梁山好汉总座次第五.en:
Jiang Jing, the Divine Calculator, corresponded to the Earthly Assembly Star and ranked fifty-third among Liangshan's 108 heroes, within the Earthly Fiends. Born in Tanzhou, Hunan, he was an unsuccessful examination candidate. A scholar with considerable strategic knowledge and mastery of calculation, he was accomplished in both civil and martial matters.

His greatest strength lay in calculation. Writing accounts and directing money and supplies were all within his command, and he knew every method of the Nine Chapters. He also understood the Six Jia's patterns of wind and clouds and the numerical principles of Heaven, Earth and Humanity. Army receipts and disbursements, stockpile dimensions and granary measurements were exact when they passed through his hands. He could calculate yin and yang, trace sun and moon and read weather, understanding changes in celestial conditions. Hence his nickname: “Divine Calculator” praised his precision and seemingly miraculous arithmetic, while the respectful suffix honored his learning and intelligence. Yet talent brought neither recognition nor success in the examinations. He abandoned that career, wandered abroad and became an outlaw.

His stronghold was Yellow Gate Mountain, where four heroes held command: Ou Peng, the Golden Wings Brushing the Clouds, first; Jiang Jing second; Ma Lin, the Iron Flute Immortal, third; and Tao Zongwang, the Nine-tailed Turtle, fourth. They raided homes and travelers and became influential around the Jiangxi-Hunan border. One day Dai Zong and Li Kui passed nearby on Liangshan business toward Jiangzhou. The followers stopped them, and the four chiefs descended intending to intercept them. Once names were exchanged and they learned these were Song Jiang's men, all responded with deep respect and hastily invited them to the stronghold.

There Dai Zong explained Liangshan's cause of acting for Heaven and gathering worthy men, along with Song Jiang's generosity toward heroes everywhere. All four longed to join. They agreed to abandon Yellow Gate Mountain, gather their men, money and grain, and travel with Dai Zong to Liangshan in a great company. Song Jiang was overjoyed by the four additions, especially Jiang Jing's accounting skills, which the stronghold urgently needed. He received them with a feast. Jiang Jing thereafter managed money and grain, calculating receipts and expenditures as the general supervisor of Liangshan's financial measures.

At the great assembly he received the Earthly Assembly Star and the fifty-third seat. His formal duty was to examine and calculate all receipts and expenditures of money and provisions, overseeing accounts, stores and distribution. Liangshan's many men required vast resources, and his precise management kept everything orderly and error-free. Though no frontline combat post, it supported the entire army's supply lifeline and was critically important. The scholar's mathematical learning enabled him to govern finances and grain, an inconspicuous but substantial service.

After the amnesty he accompanied the campaigns against Liao, Tian Hu and Wang Qing, continuing his accounts and supply calculations so that provisions and pay remained sufficient and well managed. He later crossed south with Song Jiang into Wu and Yue against Fang La. The campaign cost Liangshan dearly, but Jiang Jing's civilian financial duties kept him away from the front and allowed him to survive.

After the victory and return, seeing his brothers killed, wounded and scattered and their former splendor extinguished, Jiang Jing wished to retire. He sought no further salary or office, bade farewell and returned to Tanzhou as a prosperous local man. He died peacefully, one of the surviving officers who found a secure home. Learned and mathematically skilled, an Earthly Fiend whose merit lay in administration, he valued safety over glory and withdrew intact. His name was not made by courage in combat, but his abilities were a pillar of the marsh, Water Margin's unique master of finance and calculation.
蒋敬，绰号「神算子」，乃梁山泊一百单八将中地会星，居地煞之列，梁山好汉总座次第五.ja:
蒋敬は、あだ名を「神算子」といい、梁山泊百八人の地会星、地煞に属する第五十三位である。湖南の潭州出身で、もとは科挙に落ちた挙子だった。読書人として兵法の心得もあり、数算に精通する、文武を知る好漢だった。

長所は何より「算」にあった。帳簿と金糧の配分に通じ、九章の算法を知らぬものはなく、六甲の風雲や天地人の数理も理解した。軍の出納、積荷の寸法、倉の計量も、彼が扱えば少しの誤りもなかった。陰陽を計り、日月を推し、風雲を読んで天時の変化を知るため、神算子と呼ばれた。「神算」は緻密な思考と神のような計算、「子」は学問と知恵への敬称である。しかし才は遇されず、功名も成らず、科挙を捨てて流浪し、山賊となった。

落ち着いたのは黄門山で、頭領は四人いた。首領が摩雲金翅・欧鵬、第二が蒋敬、第三が鉄笛仙・馬麟、第四が九尾亀・陶宗旺である。家や旅商人を襲い、江西と湖南の境で勢力を張った。ある日、梁山の用務で江州方面へ向かう戴宗、李逵らが近くを通ると、手下が道を遮り、四人も迎え撃とうと下山した。しかし名を聞いて宋公明配下とわかると、皆粛然として敬い、急いで礼を尽くして寨へ招いた。

山寨では戴宗が、替天行道と人才を集める梁山の大義、宋公明が財を惜しまず天下の英雄を迎える評判を詳しく語った。四人は皆心を寄せ、黄門山を捨て、人馬と金糧をすべて集めて戴宗と梁山へ行くと決めた。大きな一行が水泊へ向かうと、宋江は四人の加入、とりわけ急に必要としていた蒋敬の算法を喜び、酒宴でもてなした。以後、蒋敬は金糧の収支を計算し、水泊の財務と計量の総管となった。

大聚義では地会星の第五十三位に座り、「金糧の支出納入を考算する」任務を担った。帳簿、倉庫、配分を総べ、人馬の多い梁山の膨大な出納は、その精密な計算によって整い、誤りなく運ばれた。突撃の武職ではないが、兵站の命脈、全軍の根本に関わる極めて重要な地位だった。一介の書生が算学をもって金糧を治めた功は、目立たずとも実に重かった。

招安後は遼、田虎、王慶との戦いに従い、引き続き金糧の計算を扱って、糧食や俸給を欠かさず、的確に配分した。方臘征討にも宋江と川を渡って南下し、呉越へ深く入った。梁山の損失は甚大だったが、財務の文職として前線の斬り合いには出ず、命を保った。

方臘平定後、兄弟の死傷と離散、栄華の消えた姿を見て、蒋敬は隠退を望んだ。官禄を求めず、一同に別れて潭州へ戻り、土地の富家として安らかに生涯を終えた。生存した将の中でも、落ち着いた帰着を得た一人である。学識と算学を胸に持ち、地煞に列して後方で功を立て、栄華を慕わず身を全うした。武勇で名を成さなくとも、才は水泊の柱であり、『水滸伝』で唯一無二の財務と計算の専門家だった。

没面目焦挺，中山府人氏，乃梁山泊一百单八将中应地恶星的好汉，坐第九十八把交椅。这.en:
Jiao Ting, the Unapproachable, came from Zhongshan and corresponded to the Earthly Evil Star, ranking ninety-eighth among Liangshan's heroes. His was a martial family that had earned its living from wrestling for three generations. In Song towns this meant two bare-chested men grappling and throwing each other in a contest of strength. Learning from childhood, Jiao Ting perfected dodges, feints, leg trips and throws until three or five ordinary strong men could not come close. His weakness was a rigid, unsociable nature. He spoke coldly, showed no friendliness and, when angered, would recognize no ties of kinship. Seeing his implacable manner, acquaintances nicknamed him Unapproachable, literally “No Face”: not a claim that he lacked features, but a reproach that he showed no consideration for relationships or worldly courtesies.

He joined Liangshan through a friendship born of a fight. When Guan Sheng led an attack on Lingzhou, Li Kui could not resist his desire for battle and secretly left the mountain alone to help. At the same time Jiao Ting was traveling to join Bao Xu, the God of Death, on Withered Tree Mountain. They met on the road. Li Kui's headstrong speech yielded nothing, and a disagreement became a fight. Confident in his strength, he dismissed the stranger, only for Jiao Ting to use the subtleties of his inherited wrestling to throw the Black Whirlwind down twice within a few exchanges. Covered in mud and water, Li Kui rose astonished. Exchanging names, they discovered they were fellow travelers toward Liangshan. Jiao Ting bowed, Li Kui admired his skill and invited him along. They later joined Bao Xu and hurried to Lingzhou, coordinating inside and outside to help capture the city. Jiao Ting then followed the others to Liangshan as a chieftain. Unlike the mountain's many men skilled in blades, bows and horses, his specialty was unarmed wrestling, giving him a distinctive place.

At the great assembly he received the Earthly Evil Star and the ninety-eighth seat as an infantry officer, often charging with the main army. He also served against Tian Hu and Wang Qing. The account records that at Nanfeng he killed the Huaixi vanguard officers Liu Yijing and Shangguan Yi, earning military merit and proving that a wrestler could also be formidable in battlefield combat.

His end, however, came early and terribly. After the amnesty, the army's southern campaign against Fang La first encountered the important position of Runzhou. During the assault, the armies collided amid trampling horses, arrows like rain and a forest of weapons. An infantryman trapped among the charging cavalry, Jiao Ting could neither advance nor withdraw. Struck, trampled and pierced by arrows, he died in the melee with scarcely an intact body. He was among the first few heroes lost after the army entered Jiangnan: they had barely reached enemy territory before losing him. The three-generation mastery of the Unapproachable never had the chance to display itself fully in the great campaign before he died beneath Runzhou. His swift and brutal departure echoed the ominous Earthly Evil Star. He is a figure whose arrival and disappearance alike carry something of his lonely, cold nature.
没面目焦挺，中山府人氏，乃梁山泊一百单八将中应地恶星的好汉，坐第九十八把交椅。这.ja:
没面目・焦挺は中山府の出身で、地悪星に応じる梁山第九十八位の好漢である。家は三代にわたって相撲を生業とする武芸の家だった。宋代の相撲とは、町場で裸の上半身を組み合わせ、力を競い、投げて勝負する角力である。幼くして家伝を継いだ焦挺は、身をかわし、誘い、脚を掛け、投げる技を極め、普通の壮漢三、五人では近寄れなかった。ただし性格は頑なで人づきあいが悪く、冷たい顔と言葉で接し、怒れば親族さえ認めず、親しみがなかった。その鉄石のような態度から、「顔がない」のではなく、情面や世間の人情を解さぬという皮肉で没面目と呼ばれた。

梁山との縁は、殴り合って知り合う形で生まれた。関勝が凌州へ出征すると、李逵は戦いたい気持ちを抑えられず、助けようと独りでこっそり下山した。一方、焦挺は枯樹山の喪門神・鮑旭へ加わろうと道を行き、二人は途中で出会った。李逵は乱暴で言葉を譲らず、口論から手が出た。力を頼んで相手を軽んじたが、焦挺は家伝の相撲で巧みに力を使い、数合もせぬうちに黒旋風を続けて二度投げ倒した。泥水まみれで起きた李逵は呆然とした。名を通じて梁山を目指す同道とわかると、焦挺は頭を下げ、李逵も腕を喜んで同行を誘った。後に鮑旭と合流し、三人で凌州へ走り、内外呼応して城の攻略を助けた。焦挺は一同と梁山へ上り、頭領となった。刀槍や弓馬ではなく、徒手の相撲という絶技を得意とする点で、山の好漢の中でも独特だった。

大聚義では地煞の地悪星、第九十八位となり、歩軍将校として本隊と突撃した。田虎や淮西の王慶の討伐にも働き、記録では南豊の戦で、淮西軍の先鋒・劉以敬と上官義を陣前に斬ったとされる。相撲の出でも、戦場の殺し合いに決して弱くなかったことがわかる。

しかし最期は非常に早く、惨かった。招安後、方臘討伐へ南下した軍の最初の要地は潤州だった。攻城戦で人馬が入り乱れ、矢が雨のように飛び、刀槍が林立する中、歩将の焦挺は奔馬の群れに取り残され、進退できなくなった。ぶつかられ、踏まれ、乱れ矢を受けてその場で死に、完全な遺体を保つのも難しかった。江南へ入った百八人のうち、最も早く失われた数人の一人である。敵地へ来たばかりで、もう彼を失った。三代伝来の相撲を大戦で存分に示す前に、潤州城下の乱軍へ消えた没面目の、速く惨い死は地悪星の凶名に応じるようだった。登場も退場も、どこか孤独で冷たい気配を帯びる人物である。

金大坚，绰号「玉臂匠」，应地煞地巧星，乃梁山泊一百单八将中第六十六位好汉，位列掌.en:
Jin Dajian, the Jade-armed Craftsman, corresponded to the Earthly Skill Star and ranked sixty-sixth among Liangshan's 108 heroes. He was the chief responsible for making military tallies and official seals. Born in Jizhou, he was a master of carving jade and stone, engraving seals and casting characters. Jade seals, documentary impressions and bronze or iron inscriptions all received exquisite workmanship, and his seal carving was unsurpassed. His hands could carve dragons and phoenixes with artistry rivaling nature, seeming as finely fashioned as beautiful jade themselves. Hence his nickname celebrated the extraordinary skill by which he became renowned.

Though a craftsman, Jin Dajian was generous and righteous and knew heroes including Dai Zong and Xiao Rang, the Sacred-handed Scholar. His arrival at Liangshan was tied to the thrilling Jiangzhou affair of trying to rescue Song Jiang with a forged letter.

After Huang Wenbing exposed Song Jiang's drunken rebellious poem at Xunyang Tower, Song was jailed and sentenced to death. Receiving Dai Zong's report, the heroes urgently sought a rescue. Wu Yong proposed forging a family letter from Grand Tutor Cai Jing to his son, Prefect Cai Jiu, ordering Song Jiang sent to the Eastern Capital. Liangshan could then seize him when the escort passed its territory. The forgery required two skills: copying Cai Jing's writing and reproducing his seal. Xiao Rang, adept in the styles of Su, Huang, Mi and Cai, would handle the handwriting. For a master engraver, Wu Yong chose Jin Dajian of Jizhou.

Using his swift traveling art, Dai Zong tricked both craftsmen into coming to Liangshan. Only upon arrival did they learn that they were needed to forge Cai Jing's letter and save Song Jiang. Xiao Rang copied the script and Jin Dajian reproduced the seal so convincingly that the result seemed genuine. Yet their careful planning contained a fatal oversight: why would Cai Jing use a private inscription seal in correspondence with his own son? Wu Yong and the craftsmen had chosen the wrong kind of seal. When the letter reached Jiangzhou, the meticulous Huang Wenbing detected the flaw, exposing it and bringing both Song Jiang and Dai Zong near death on the execution ground. Only Liangshan's raid, with Li Kui and the others fighting their way in, saved them. Having participated in the forgery, Xiao Rang and Jin Dajian had no retreat and joined Liangshan together.

Jin Dajian's craft found its proper use on the mountain. Military tallies, command tokens, seals, official impressions and all the credentials needed for correspondence were carved and made by him. He and Xiao Rang, one writing and the other engraving, formed a perfectly matched team managing the stronghold's documents and seals. This technical expertise was indispensable. At the assembly he received the Earthly Skill Star and the sixty-sixth seat, formally charged with all military tallies and seals, a fitting position earned through craft.

After the amnesty he accompanied the army's campaigns. As a civilian craftsman rather than a battlefield officer, he mostly continued handling seals and documents during the wars against Liao, Tian Hu, Wang Qing and Fang La, without personally braving arrows and stones in bloody combat. In the Fang La campaign, where seven or eight in ten heroes were lost, his noncombatant role allowed him to survive and return with the army.

After victory the court distributed rewards. His extraordinary engraving became famous in the capital, and the emperor retained him in the Imperial Seal Office within the palace administration to make royal seals, treasured impressions and official markings. The former Liangshan craftsman thus reached a fortunate ending, winning a secure future with his capable hands. Amid a conclusion filled with blood, tears and overwhelming losses, this was a rare good outcome. Later storytellers observed that Jin Dajian established himself through a single craft, moved comfortably between advancement and withdrawal, and preserved both life and name, a distinctive figure among the heroes.
金大坚，绰号「玉臂匠」，应地煞地巧星，乃梁山泊一百单八将中第六十六位好汉，位列掌.ja:
金大堅は、あだ名を「玉臂匠」といい、地煞の地巧星に応じる第六十六位で、兵符と印信の製作を専ら担う頭領だった。済州出身の、玉石の彫刻、印刻、文字の鋳造に優れた職人である。金石篆刻の妙を極め、玉石の印、文書の図印、銅鉄の碑も精巧に刻み、特に印章では当代に冠たる腕を持った。竜や鳳凰を彫る両手は、天工を奪うほど巧みで、美玉で作ったかのようだったため、玉臂匠と呼ばれた。一芸によって世に知られた奇人である。

職人の出でも、金大堅は義に厚く財を惜しまず、戴宗、聖手書生・蕭譲ら江湖の好漢と交わっていた。梁山へ入る原因は、江州の胸を揺さぶる事件、「偽書で宋江を救う」策だった。

宋江は潯陽楼で酔って反詩を書き、黄文炳に訴えられ、江州の牢で斬首を待っていた。戴宗の報告を受けた梁山は救済を急ぎ、呉用が蔡京の家書を偽造する策を立てた。息子の蔡九知府へ宋江を東京に送るよう命じれば、梁山の領域を通る途中で奪えるというのである。これには蔡京の筆跡と印をまねる二つの技が要った。蘇、黄、米、蔡の四家の書体に巧みな蕭譲が文字を担当し、印刻の名手として呉用が挙げたのが、済州の金大堅だった。

戴宗は神行法を使って二人を計略で山へ連れて来た。事情を知らなかった二人は、到着して初めて、蔡京の書状を偽造して宋江を救う手助けと知った。蕭譲が筆をまね、金大堅が見本どおりに印を彫ると、本物と見まがう出来になった。だが綿密な相談にも一つの穴があった。父が息子へ出す手紙に、なぜ図書の私印を使うのか、という印の種類の誤りである。江州に届くと細心な黄文炳が見破り、宋江と戴宗は逆に絶境へ追い込まれ、刑場で命を失う寸前となった。梁山の好漢が襲い、李逵らが斬り込んでようやく救えた。偽造に加わった蕭譲と金大堅も、すでに退路がなく、ともに梁山へ帰順した。

入山後は技にふさわしい仕事を得た。兵符、将令、印信、図印、対外文書の印や証明は、すべて彼が彫り、作った。書く蕭譲と刻む金大堅は珠玉のように組み合い、山寨の文書と印鑑を担う欠かせぬ技術者となった。席次では地巧星の第六十六位を得て、兵符印信の専任となり、まさしく巧技で身を立てた。

招安後は大軍と南北を征討したが、文職の職人であって戦闘の将ではないため、遼、田虎、王慶、方臘との戦いでも、多くは本職の印信と文書を扱った。自ら矢石を冒して血戦することはなく、好漢の十に七、八を失った方臘征討でも命を保ち、軍とともに帰還した。

凱旋後、論功行賞の際には絶妙な彫刻の名が都に広まり、御前に留め置かれた。内府の御宝監へ入り、朝廷の御用の印璽や宝鑑、図印を彫るよう命じられたのである。梁山の職人頭領は、巧みな両手で安定した前途を得て、生涯を全うした。血涙と大損失に満ちる結末の中では、貴重な善果だった。後世の語り手も、一芸で身を立て、進退に余裕を持ち、最後に身と名を保った金大堅を、好漢の中でも独特の人物と評している。

孔亮，绰号「独火星」，应地煞地狂星，乃梁山泊一百单八将中第六十三位好汉，与其兄孔.en:
Kong Liang, nicknamed “Solitary Fire Star,” answered to the Earthly Wild Star and ranked sixty-third among the 108 heroes of Liangshan Marsh. He and his elder brother Kong Ming were known as the Two Heroes of the Kong Family; both served as junior cavalry commanders and leaders of long-range scouts. A native of Kong Family Village beneath White Tiger Mountain in Qingzhou, Kong Liang shared his brother's standing as a local strongman. Impatient, fierce, and full of fire, he insisted on winning every dispute, earning his nickname in the martial world. “Solitary Fire” likened his temper to a lone, fiercely burning flame. It matched the disposition of his brother, the Shaggy-Headed Star: both were explosive, blunt men who could flare up at a touch, and nobody in the district dared provoke them.

The brothers originally owned an estate near White Tiger Mountain. Relying on Old Master Kong's property and wealth, they dominated the countryside. A feud with a local rich man led them to murder his entire household. Having committed a crime of terrible magnitude and finding nowhere to hide, they occupied White Tiger Mountain, gathered estate retainers and fugitives, and became bandits who raided homes and robbed travelers. Before Song Jiang rose to prominence, while seeking refuge in the martial world, he had once rested and sheltered at Old Master Kong's estate. Kong Ming and Kong Liang had long admired his reputation for generosity and loyalty. They became his pupils and learned spear and staff techniques from him. This bond between teacher and pupils laid the foundation for their later allegiance to Liangshan.

Much of Kong Liang's skill with spear and staff came directly from Song Jiang's instruction, and he was a capable fighting officer in the cavalry. Of the two brothers, he was somewhat more adaptable than Kong Ming and could still find a way around difficulties instead of relying entirely on recklessness. Yet his “Solitary Fire” nature remained fierce and untamed: once he entered a quarrel or a fight, he would not readily concede defeat.

The story of his arrival at Liangshan began with a disaster in Qingzhou. The brothers had become enemies of Prefect Murong. Impatient to settle their old grievance, Kong Ming led their retainers against the city, but government troops defeated him and captured him alive. He was thrown into Qingzhou's prison. Kong Liang escaped the rout by good fortune and, with no one else to appeal to, traveled through the night toward Twin Dragons Mountain. An incident interrupted his flight: a dispute in a roadside tavern brought him face to face with Wu Song the Pilgrim. Kong Liang was no match for him and received a humiliating beating. After Wu Song questioned him, they discovered their shared connection to Song Jiang and that both were men in distress. Their hostility gave way to friendship. Wu Song introduced him to Lu Zhishen, Yang Zhi, and the other heroes at Twin Dragons Mountain, where he begged them to send troops to rescue his brother.

Song Jiang, himself on his way to Liangshan, happened to pass through the district and meet the assembled heroes. Kong Liang tearfully told him that his brother lay in prison with his life in danger. Song Jiang could hardly stand aside while a cherished pupil suffered. He therefore brought together the heroes of Twin Dragons Mountain, Peach Blossom Mountain, and White Tiger Mountain, along with a large Liangshan force, to attack Qingzhou. After hard fighting they tricked the defenders into opening the gates, entered the city, killed Prefect Murong, broke into the prison, and freed Kong Ming. With Qingzhou taken and its wicked official executed, the heroes of the three mountains decided to unite and go to Liangshan together. Indebted to their teacher for saving them and with nowhere else to settle, the brothers followed Song Jiang to Liangshan Marsh with wholehearted devotion.

When the brotherhood assigned its ranks, Kong Liang took the sixty-third seat as the Earthly Wild Star. He and Kong Ming both became junior cavalry commanders and leaders of long-range scouts, responsible for reconnaissance, patrols, and fighting charges. During the subsequent campaigns against Liao, Tian Hu, and Wang Qing, Kong Liang served faithfully in the ranks. Though he never independently commanded an entire front or army, he repeatedly faced blades and spears, fought bravely at the fore, and earned merit beside his brother.

The final campaign against Fang La brought exceptionally savage fighting in Jiangnan, where more than half the Liangshan brothers were lost. Kong Liang advanced with the army but drowned during a river crossing, his body left to the fish, and never saw the day of victory. His elder brother Kong Ming also died of illness at Liuhe Temple in Hangzhou. The Two Heroes of the Kong Family had stood together at White Tiger Mountain and followed Song Jiang through campaigns north and south; in the end, one died sick and the other drowned. Both left their bones in Jiangnan and neither reached a peaceful end. The fiery brothers who once dominated the foot of White Tiger Mountain became two loyal spirits in Water Margin's pages of lament, leaving later readers to sigh at their fate.
孔亮，绰号「独火星」，应地煞地狂星，乃梁山泊一百单八将中第六十三位好汉，与其兄孔.ja:
孔亮は「独火星」の異名を持ち、地煞の地狂星に応じる、梁山泊百八将の第六十三位の好漢である。兄の孔明とともに「孔家の二雄」と称され、二人とも馬軍小彪将兼遠探出哨頭領を務めた。青州の白虎山の麓にある孔家荘の出身で、兄と同じく土地の豪強であった。気性はせっかちで激しく、常に火のような怒りを抱き、何事にも勝ちを求めたため、江湖で「独火星」と呼ばれた。「独火」とは、孤立して燃え盛る炎のように激しく手に負えない性質をいう。兄の「毛頭星」の気性とよく似ており、二人とも短気で一本気、少し触れれば爆発するような男だったので、郷里では誰も逆らおうとしなかった。

兄弟はもともと白虎山一帯の荘園主で、父の孔太公の土地と財力を頼みに村里を支配していた。やがて地元の富豪と仇敵となり、その一家を皆殺しにしてしまう。取り返しのつかない大罪を犯して身の置き所を失い、白虎山を占拠し、荘客や命知らずを集めて山賊となり、家々を襲い略奪を働いた。宋江がまだ世に出ず、江湖で難を避けていた頃、孔太公の荘園に立ち寄って身を休めたことがあった。孔明と孔亮は、義を重んじ財を惜しまぬ宋江の名声をかねて慕っており、弟子となって槍棒の武芸を学んだ。この師弟の縁こそ、後に兄弟が梁山泊へ帰順する根となった。

孔亮の槍棒の技も、その多くが宋江の直伝であり、馬軍の中で一員の戦将と呼べる腕前だった。兄弟を比べると、孔亮の方が孔明よりいくらか機転が利き、物事に融通をつける余地があって、兄のようにひたすら向こう見ずではなかった。しかし「独火」の本性はやはり激しく抑え難く、人と争えば容易には負けを認めなかった。

孔亮が梁山泊へ上る経緯は、青州で起きた大難から始まる。当時、兄弟は青州の慕容知府と仇を結んでいた。気の早い孔明は荘客の軍勢を率い、旧怨を晴らそうと青州を攻めたが、逆に官軍に敗れ、生け捕りにされて青州の牢へ入れられた。孔亮は乱軍の中を幸運にも逃れたものの、ほかに助けを求める先もなく、夜を日に継いで二竜山へ向かった。その途上には一つの挿話がある。道端の居酒屋で争いを起こし、思いがけず行者武松に出会ったのである。手合わせしても武松にかなうはずはなく、散々に打ち負かされた。事情を尋ねられ、どちらも宋江につながる者で、同じく難に遭っている身だと分かり、ようやく争いを収めた。武松の紹介で二竜山に上り、魯智深や楊志らの豪傑に会い、兄を救うため兵を出してほしいと頼んだ。

折しも宋江も梁山泊へ向かう途中でこの地を通り、好漢たちと合流した。孔亮は、兄が牢につながれ命も危ういと涙ながらに訴えた。愛弟子の難を聞いた宋江が手をこまねいているはずもない。二竜山、桃花山、白虎山の英雄たちと梁山泊の大軍を集め、青州を共に攻めた。苦戦の末に計略で城門を開かせ、城内へ突入して慕容知府を斬り、牢を破って孔明を救い出した。青州が落ち悪官が処刑されると、三山の好漢は一つにまとまり、そろって梁山泊へ上り大義に集うことを決めた。恩師に救われ、ほかに身を寄せる先もない孔亮兄弟は、心から忠誠を誓って宋江に従った。

聚義の席次が定まると、孔亮は地狂星、第六十三位となった。兄の孔明とともに馬軍小彪将兼遠探出哨頭領に任じられ、偵察や突撃、巡察などを担った。その後の南征北伐、遼国、田虎、王慶との戦いにも軍中で力を尽くした。一方面を独力で守り、一軍を統率する大将ではなかったが、幾度も刀槍の下をくぐり、勇んで先陣に立ち、兄と肩を並べて功を立てた。

最後の方臘征討はことに凄惨で、江南の戦いで梁山の兄弟は半数以上を失った。孔亮も軍に従って進んだが、ある渡河の折に不幸にも水へ落ちて溺死し、魚の餌食となり、凱旋の日を見ることはなかった。兄の孔明も杭州の六和寺で病没した。孔家の二雄は白虎山で心を合わせ、宋公明に従って南北を転戦した末、一人は病み、一人は溺れ、いずれも江南に骨を埋めて安らかな最期を得られなかった。かつて白虎山の麓で一方に威を振るった激しい兄弟は、悲歌に満ちた水滸の物語の中で二つの忠魂となり、後の読者に無念のため息をつかせるのである。

孔明，绰号「毛头星」，应地煞地猖星，乃梁山泊一百单八将中第六十二位好汉，与其弟孔.en:
Kong Ming, nicknamed “Shaggy-Headed Star,” answered to the Earthly Rampant Star and ranked sixty-second among the 108 heroes of Liangshan Marsh. He and his younger brother Kong Liang were called the Two Heroes of the Kong Family, and both served as junior cavalry commanders and leaders of long-range scouts. Born in Kong Family Village beneath White Tiger Mountain in Qingzhou, Kong Ming and his brother were local tyrants. His fiery temper, habit of rushing into trouble and fighting at the slightest provocation, and mass of untidy hair earned him the nickname Shaggy-Headed Star. The name also suggested his reckless haste and lack of restraint: the smallest spark could set him ablaze.

The brothers had originally dominated the Qingzhou countryside through their estate and retainers. In a rage over a feud with a local rich man, they killed his entire household, old and young. Guilty of murder, they gathered a band on White Tiger Mountain and became robber chiefs, raiding homes and plundering. They already had a close connection to Liangshan's leader Song Jiang. Back when Song Jiang was still a clerk in Yuncheng and had not yet fallen into trouble, he had spent some time seeking refuge at Old Master Kong's estate. During that stay, Kong Ming and Kong Liang, who admired his reputation, became his pupils and learned spear and staff techniques. Song Jiang was thus the respected teacher of the Two Heroes of the Kong Family, and this bond later brought them into Liangshan's ranks.

Much of Kong Ming's martial skill came from Song Jiang's guidance. He could ride unruly horses and wield a long spear, making him a seasoned and capable cavalry officer. Yet he had more courage than strategy and was rash by nature, repeatedly acting on hot blood alone. He lacked even the modest adaptability of his younger brother. During their time at White Tiger Mountain, the two often fought over the smallest grudges: once the temper of the “Shaggy Head” or “Solitary Fire” erupted, it was hard to stop.

His path to Liangshan turned on an upheaval in Qingzhou. Having fallen into a feud with Prefect Murong, Kong Ming led his retainers to attack Qingzhou and settle the old score. Outnumbered, he instead suffered a crushing defeat at the hands of government troops, was taken alive, and was thrown into the city's prison with his life hanging by a thread. Kong Liang escaped by chance and hurried away to seek help. Lu Zhishen the Tattooed Monk, Yang Zhi the Blue-Faced Beast, Wu Song the Pilgrim, and their companions were then living as outlaws at Twin Dragons Mountain, so Kong Liang went there for reinforcements. By coincidence, Song Jiang was also on his way to Liangshan and met the heroes while passing through. Hearing that his beloved pupil Kong Ming was imprisoned, he could not stand idly by. He joined forces with the heroes of Twin Dragons Mountain, Peach Blossom Mountain, and White Tiger Mountain to attack Qingzhou.

Heroes from every side gathered for the great battle, making an imposing force. Troops of Song Jiang's Liangshan Marsh army were also called in, and Qin Ming the Thunderbolt, Hua Rong the Little Li Guang, and others all came to help. Acting together inside and outside the city, they first tricked the defenders into opening the gates, then stormed Qingzhou, killed Prefect Murong, broke open the prison, and rescued Kong Ming. After the fighting the city had fallen and its wicked official was dead. The heroes of the three mountains then agreed to go to Liangshan together and unite in the common cause. Saved by their teacher and with nowhere else to live, Kong Ming and Kong Liang naturally followed Song Jiang to Liangshan Marsh with unwavering loyalty.

After the brotherhood assembled and assigned its seats, Kong Ming ranked sixty-second as the Earthly Rampant Star. He and Kong Liang both served as junior cavalry commanders and leaders of long-range scouts. They were responsible for reconnaissance, patrols, and charges into enemy formations; whenever intelligence had to be carried or fighting broke out at the outposts, the brothers were often first forward. Kong Ming subsequently served throughout the campaigns against Liao, Tian Hu, and Wang Qing. Though never a great commander entrusted with an independent army or front, he fought repeatedly and never shrank back.

During the campaign against Fang La, the Jiangnan fighting left Liangshan's heroes heaped among the dead and wounded, with seven or eight in ten lost. Kong Ming contracted a grave illness amid the campaign and could no longer march. He and other sick comrades were left to recover at Liuhe Temple in Hangzhou. But an epidemic spread through the army, and he never rose from his sickbed. He died in the temple before he could see the army return victorious. It was a sorrowful end for the Shaggy-Headed Star, whose half-lifetime of fiery energy ended in illness. His younger brother Kong Liang drowned while crossing a river on the campaign. One died sick and the other by drowning: neither of the Two Heroes of the Kong Family met a peaceful end, and both their spirits remained in Jiangnan, to the grief of all who heard their story.
孔明，绰号「毛头星」，应地煞地猖星，乃梁山泊一百单八将中第六十二位好汉，与其弟孔.ja:
孔明は「毛頭星」の異名を持ち、地煞の地猖星に応じる、梁山泊百八将の第六十二位の好漢である。弟の孔亮とともに「孔家の二雄」と称され、二人とも馬軍小彪将兼遠探出哨頭領に名を連ねた。青州の白虎山の麓、孔家荘の出身で、弟と同じく土地の顔役であった。性は烈火のごとく、短気で何事にも突き進み、すぐに人と激しく争った。髪もぼさぼさに乱れていたため、江湖では「毛頭星」と呼ばれた。「毛頭」には向こう見ずでせっかち、慎みを知らぬという意味もあり、少し火をつければ燃え上がる本人の気性そのものだった。

孔明と孔亮は、もとは青州一帯に威を振るう兄弟で、家の荘園と荘客を頼みに村里を横行していた。地元の富豪と仇を結び、怒りに任せてその一家を老若ともに皆殺しにしたため、人命を奪う罪を犯し、白虎山に仲間を集めて家々を襲う山賊の頭となった。二人は梁山泊の頭領宋江とも深い縁があった。宋江がまだ鄆城で押司を務め、難に落ちる前の頃、孔太公の荘園で難を避け、しばらく滞在したことがある。その間、名声を慕う兄弟は宋江に弟子入りし、槍棒の武芸を学んだ。したがって宋江は孔家の二雄の恩師であり、この師弟の情が後の梁山泊帰順へつながった。

孔明の槍棒の腕は宋江の指導によるところが大きく、荒馬を乗りこなし長槍を使う、馬軍でも戦慣れた将の一人だった。しかし勇気はあっても知略に乏しく、気性も粗暴で、往々にして血気だけで行動した。多少は機転の利く弟の孔亮にも及ばなかった。白虎山にいた頃の兄弟は、わずかな恨みや些細な事でもよく人と争い、「毛頭」と「独火」の性分が一度噴き出せば、収拾がつかなかった。

孔明が梁山泊へ上ることになったのは、青州での騒動による。当時、兄弟は慕容知府と仇を結んでいた。孔明は荘客の軍勢を率い、旧恨を晴らそうと青州城を攻めたが、多勢に無勢で官軍に大敗した。自らも生け捕りにされて青州の大牢へ送られ、命は朝夕にも危うかった。孔亮は幸運にも逃れ、慌てて助けを求めた。この頃、花和尚魯智深、青面獣楊志、行者武松らが二竜山に集まって山賊となっており、孔亮はそこへ援軍を頼みに上った。折よく宋江も梁山泊へ向かおうとしてこの地を通り、好漢たちと会った。愛弟子孔明が牢にあると聞いて黙っていることはできず、二竜山、桃花山、白虎山の豪傑たちを合わせ、青州を攻めることにした。

青州の大戦には各地の好漢が雲のように集まり、その勢いは盛大だった。さらに梁山泊の宋公明の軍勢にも援軍を頼み、霹靂火秦明、小李広花栄らもこぞって加わった。皆が力を合わせて内外から呼応し、まず計略で城門を開かせ、青州へ攻め込んだ。慕容知府を斬り、大牢を破り、孔明を救い出す。激戦の末に青州城は落ち、悪官は罪に伏した。その後、三山の豪傑は相談し、いっそ共に梁山泊へ上って大義に集おうと決めた。恩師に救われ、ほかに居場所のない孔明と孔亮は、当然ながら心から帰服し、宋江に従って梁山泊へ向かった。

聚義の後に席次が定められ、孔明は地猖星、第六十二位となった。弟とともに馬軍小彪将兼遠探出哨頭領を務め、偵察や巡回、敵陣への突撃を担った。軍情の伝達や前哨の戦闘では、兄弟がしばしば先頭に立った。その後も大軍に従って南北を転戦し、遼国、田虎、王慶の征討で力を尽くした。一方面を任される大将ではなかったが、幾度も戦いを重ね、一度も尻込みしなかった。

方臘征討の江南の戦いでは梁山の好漢が死傷して累々と重なり、十人のうち七、八人が失われた。孔明も戦乱の中で重病にかかり、軍と共に進めなくなったため、病む仲間とともに杭州の六和寺へ残されて療養した。ところが軍中には疫病が広まり、孔明は病床から起き上がれず、そのまま六和寺で世を去り、凱旋の日を見ることはなかった。半生を激しい気性で生きた「毛頭星」が病床で果てたのは、まことに痛ましい。弟の孔亮は遠征中の渡河で溺死した。孔家の二雄は一人が病み、一人が溺れ、いずれも安らかな最期を迎えられず魂を江南へ帰し、聞く者を嘆かせたのである。

雷横，绰号「插翅虎」，应天退星，梁山泊英雄座次第二十五位。其人本贯山东郓城县人氏.en:
Lei Heng, nicknamed “Winged Tiger,” answered to the Heavenly Retreating Star and held the twenty-fifth seat among Liangshan Marsh's heroes. He came from Yuncheng County in Shandong, where his family had worked as blacksmiths for generations. Their considerable farmland and his position as a county constable made him well known locally. Seven chi tall, with a purplish-red face, he usually carried a pudao at his waist and was skilled with a three-pointed, double-edged spear. He could leap walls and climb dangerous heights with extraordinary agility, as though wings grew from his body, earning him the name Winged Tiger. Upright and resolute, he valued loyalty above wealth, though he also had the faults of rough impatience and temperamental behavior over money. He was a typical blunt-spoken Shandong hero.

As Yuncheng's infantry constable, Lei Heng was paired with the mounted constable Zhu Tong. The two were renowned together, one measured and the other martial, their qualities complementing each other. Zhu Tong was generous and considerate; Lei Heng was fierce and proud. Both were close friends of the clerk Song Jiang. When Chao Gai and six companions were exposed as the men who had taken the birthday gifts by stratagem, Jizhou sent the arrest officer He Tao to Yuncheng. The magistrate ordered Zhu Tong and Lei Heng to lead separate parties and surround Chao Gai's estate in Dongxi Village. Lei Heng attacked the front gate with his infantry while Zhu Tong secretly left Chao Gai an escape through the rear. Lei Heng won no chief credit but did not pursue the matter closely, showing the longstanding ties between these constables and the future Liangshan brotherhood. There was another earlier incident: on a village patrol at night, Lei Heng arrested a naked, powerfully built man in Lingguan Temple. This was Liu Tang, later the Red-Haired Demon, who had come to join Chao Gai and propose seizing the birthday gifts. Bound by Lei Heng and about to be brought before the authorities, he was rescued when Chao Gai claimed him as his nephew. This led into the great story of the seven stars joining in brotherhood.

A killing drove Lei Heng into outlawry. A family of performers had newly arrived in Yuncheng from the entertainment quarters of the Eastern Capital. Among them was a courtesan singer named Bai Xiuying, intimate with the magistrate, who used his patronage while performing near the county office. One day Lei Heng had no money on him to offer a tip, and Bai Xiuying subjected him to repeated insults and mockery. Unable to swallow the affront, he quarreled with her on the spot. The next day she also insulted his mother. Furious, he swung the end of his cangue into Bai Xiuying's temple and killed her. The magistrate was enraged and insisted that Lei Heng be condemned to death and sent under escort. His escort happened to be his benefactor Zhu Tong. Remembering that Lei Heng was a worthy man with an aged mother still living, Zhu Tong secretly freed him in an isolated place and took the immense consequences on himself. For this, Zhu Tong was tattooed and exiled to Cangzhou. With every other road closed, Lei Heng went to join Liangshan Marsh.

Once on the mountain, his accomplished martial skills and readiness to fight placed him among the swift cavalry and vanguard commanders. He often led charges into enemy formations. Skilled with the three-pointed, double-edged blade and the pudao alike, he could fight either on foot or horseback. He gained successes in the battles at Zhu Family Village, Gaotangzhou, Qingzhou, and Huazhou, working with infantry and cavalry leaders to earn merit. When the great brotherhood assigned its Heavenly and Earthly Star rankings, his place among the Heavenly Stars as the Heavenly Retreating Star showed the weight he carried in the stronghold.

After Song Jiang accepted imperial amnesty, Lei Heng followed the army north and south. In the Liao campaign he fought bravely at the front, helped defeat enemy troops and take cities, and earned military merit. He later survived the campaigns against Tian Hu and Wang Qing as well. The most terrible losses came in the expedition against Fang La. With Fang La commanding numerous troops and generals in Jiangnan, more than half the Liangshan heroes fell. Lei Heng joined the attack on Deqing County and faced Fang La's officer Si Xingfang. He fought stubbornly without retreat, but whether because his horse stumbled or because his strength failed him, Si Xingfang cut him down with a single stroke. Dying in imperial service, the Shandong hero met a soldier's end, his body wrapped in horsehide. His filial concern for his aged mother, his connection to Liu Tang's release, and the fierce anger that killed the courtesan with his cangue all passed into the memory of a loyal soul. When Song Jiang returned, the fallen were honored according to their service, and Lei Heng received posthumous military distinctions of the Zhongwulang kind. Enshrined among Liangshan's heroic dead, the Winged Tiger was remembered for a lifetime of integrity and loyalty.
雷横，绰号「插翅虎」，应天退星，梁山泊英雄座次第二十五位。其人本贯山东郓城县人氏.ja:
雷横は「挿翅虎」の異名を持ち、天退星に応じる梁山泊第二十五位の英雄である。本貫は山東の鄆城県で、家は代々鍛冶を営んでいた。かなりの田畑を持つうえ、自身も県の都頭を務めていたため、郷里でよく知られていた。身の丈七尺、顔は紫がかった赤色で、腰にはいつも朴刀を帯び、三尖両刃槍も得意とした。塀や壁を飛び越え、高所や険しい場所へ赴く身のこなしは並外れており、まるで背に翼があるようだったので、江湖で「挿翅虎」と呼ばれた。剛直で果断、義を重んじ財を惜しまない反面、粗野でせっかち、金銭をめぐって気性を荒らす欠点もあり、山東の好漢らしい一本気な男だった。

鄆城県では歩兵都頭を務め、馬兵都頭の朱仝と二雄と称された。一人は穏やか、一人は武張って、互いを補う間柄である。朱仝は寛大で気配りに富み、雷横は激しく意気を尊んだが、二人とも押司宋江と親しかった。晁蓋ら七人が生辰綱を計略で奪ったことが発覚すると、済州府は捕縛を担当する観察の何濤を鄆城へ派遣した。知県は朱仝と雷横にそれぞれ兵を率いさせ、東渓村の晁蓋の荘園を包囲させた。雷横が歩兵を率いて表門を攻める一方、朱仝は裏門から密かに晁蓋を逃がした。雷横は手柄を得られなかったが深く追及せず、二人の都頭と梁山の一派には早くから縁があったことが分かる。また、それ以前の夜回りでは、霊官廟で裸のたくましい大男を捕らえたことがあった。後の「赤髪鬼」劉唐である。生辰綱を奪う仲間になろうと晁蓋を訪ねてきたところを縛られ、役所へ送られかけたが、晁蓋が甥だと偽って引き取ったため救われた。この一件から七星聚義の大きな物語が始まる。

雷横が山賊となった原因は、一件の殺人だった。東京の演芸場から鄆城へ新たに来た芸人一家に、白秀英という歌妓がいた。知県と親しい彼女はその威を借り、県役所の前の小屋で歌っていた。ある日、雷横は手元に祝儀の金がなく、白秀英から散々罵られ、からかわれた。屈辱をこらえきれず、その場で争いとなる。翌日、白秀英が雷横の母まで侮辱すると、怒りを爆発させた雷横は首枷の端を振り上げ、そのこめかみを打って殺してしまった。知県は激怒し、どうしても死罪にしようと護送を命じた。その護送役が恩人の朱仝だった。雷横が好漢で、家には老母がいることを思い、朱仝は人目のない場所で密かに逃がし、自ら大きな責任を引き受けた。このため朱仝は入墨刑を受け、滄州へ流された。行き場を失った雷横は、梁山泊へ上って仲間となった。

入山後は武芸に熟達し、戦場で恐れず戦うことから、馬軍驃騎兼先鋒使の頭領に列せられ、しばしば突撃を担った。三尖両刃刀を使い、朴刀にも巧みで、徒歩でも騎馬でも戦えた。祝家荘、高唐州、青州、華州などの攻略で戦果を挙げ、歩軍や馬軍の頭領たちと協力して功を立てた。梁山の大聚義で天罡地煞の席次を決めると、天退星として天罡に列したことからも、山寨での重みがうかがえる。

宋江が招安を受けると、雷横も軍に従って南北を征した。遼国との戦いでは陣前で奮戦し、仲間と遼軍を破り城を落として軍功を立てた。その後の田虎、王慶征討でも南北を転戦し、無事に生き残った。最も凄惨だったのは方臘征討である。江南の方臘は兵も将も多く、梁山の好漢は半数以上を失った。雷横は徳清県の攻略に加わり、敵将司行方と対陣した。力を尽くして退かなかったが、馬が前脚を踏み外したためか、力が及ばなかったためか、ついに司行方の一刀で馬上から斬り落とされ、王事に殉じた。山東の好漢は軍馬の革に遺体を包まれる武人の最期を遂げたのである。老母への孝心も、劉唐を逃がした縁も、首枷で歌妓を打った激しさも、ここに歴史に残る一筋の忠魂となった。宋江の凱旋後、戦功に応じて追叙が行われ、雷横にも忠武郎の類の戦没者への追封が与えられた。梁山の英烈とともに祀られ、後人は「挿翅虎」の剛直と忠義の生涯を偲ぶこととなった。

李衮，绰号「飞天大圣」，应地煞地走星，乃梁山泊一百单八将中第六十五位好汉，位列步.en:
Li Gun, nicknamed “Heaven-Flying Great Sage,” answered to the Earthly Running Star and ranked sixty-fifth among Liangshan Marsh's 108 heroes. An infantry commander, he came to Liangshan with Xiang Chong and Fan Rui from Mount Mangdang. He was a native of Pi County, agile, brave, and swift of foot, skilled with a round shield, throwing knives, and javelins. His abilities resembled Xiang Chong's: he carried a round shield bristling with knives and javelins on his back, whirled his shield like a gale, and hurled blades and spears at enemies several paces away. Especially gifted at running and leaping, he darted through the press of battle with astonishing speed, almost as if riding clouds. His nickname praised this lightness and swiftness; he truly came and went like the wind, difficult to catch or predict.

Li Gun and Xiang Chong were close friends, both fugitive heroes from the Xuzhou and Pizhou region. Their crimes left them nowhere to settle, so they went together to Mount Mangdang and joined Fan Rui, the Demon King of Chaos, who practiced sorcery. Fan Rui became chief, with Xiang Chong and Li Gun as his two deputies. The three occupied the mountain, gathered desperate men, and raided and robbed. With Fan Rui's arts of summoning wind and rain and the two deputies' exceptional shield and throwing-knife skills, their combined force grew formidable. They began to dream of annexing Liangshan Marsh and seizing its stronghold, publicly boasting that they would attack the mountain. Thus they provoked a feud with Liangshan.

When Song Jiang heard their boast, he mustered troops and personally marched against Mount Mangdang. Gongsun Sheng accompanied him, saying that Fan Rui's unorthodox magic could be broken by the true arts of the Five Thunders. When the armies faced each other, Li Gun and Xiang Chong led the attack. Whirling their round shields and rolling forward close to the ground, they hurled knives and javelins into Song Jiang's formation, spinning left and right like windmills with almost irresistible force. They nearly wounded Song Jiang himself. Fortunately, Lu Fang and Guo Sheng thrust out their paired halberds and fought hard to protect him, while Gongsun Sheng secretly prepared spells and concealed pits. Carried away by the fighting, Li Gun and Xiang Chong failed to watch their footing. Both tumbled into the pits, where ambushers captured them alive with hooks and ropes and brought them to the command tent.

Admiring their extraordinary courage, Song Jiang could not bear to harm them. He personally untied them, invited them into his tent, served them wine, and reassured them kindly. He explained his wish to carry out Heaven's justice and gather worthy men in brotherhood, urging them to join. The two were straightforward men. Moved by his courtesy and lack of malice, they bowed in submission and gladly agreed. They then volunteered to return to Mount Mangdang and persuade Fan Rui. Back on the mountain, they recounted Song Jiang's benevolence and generosity in full. When Fan Rui subsequently fought a magical duel with Gongsun Sheng, his sorcery was completely overcome by the orthodox arts. Convinced at last, and urged earnestly by Xiang Chong and Li Gun, he brought the entire Mount Mangdang force to Liangshan. From then on the three shared the great stronghold in complete trust and never parted ways.

When the seats were assigned, Li Gun ranked sixty-fifth as the Earthly Running Star, serving as an infantry commander alongside Xiang Chong. Their round shields and throwing knives made them ideally suited to lead assaults, break through lines, and storm defenses. In the fiercest battles they often charged first to throw the enemy into confusion, forming a uniquely bold pair of vanguard fighters in Liangshan's infantry. During the later campaigns against Liao, Tian Hu, and Wang Qing, Li Gun repeatedly fought at the front and earned distinction. He and his dear friend Xiang Chong remained inseparable, facing their enemies shoulder to shoulder.

The Jiangnan campaign against Fang La was the cruelest of all. When the army advanced into Shezhou, Li Gun and Xiang Chong led the infantry charge as usual, only to enter an enemy ambush. On the narrow, dangerous mountain road, their shields and throwing knives could not be used to full effect. Encircled, they could neither advance nor withdraw. Li Gun fought desperately but was overwhelmed by numbers and died under the blades and spears of the enemy. The Heaven-Flying Great Sage, who had spent his life moving like flight and sweeping through formations behind his shield, met his defeat in Jiangnan's treacherous terrain. He and his sworn friend Xiang Chong died in the same campaign without seeing the army return victorious to court. They had joined in brotherhood at Mount Mangdang, gone to Liangshan together, fought across the land together, and finally died in the same place. Their fidelity endured through life and death. The depth of their friendship and violence of their end form one of the most moving passages among Water Margin's tragic fates, leaving later readers in tears over these brothers who gave their lives for loyalty.
李衮，绰号「飞天大圣」，应地煞地走星，乃梁山泊一百单八将中第六十五位好汉，位列步.ja:
李袞は「飛天大聖」の異名を持ち、地煞の地走星に応じる、梁山泊百八将の第六十五位の好漢である。歩軍頭領に列し、項充、樊瑞とともに芒碭山の一隊から梁山泊へ帰順した。邳県の出身で、身のこなしは軽く、勇敢で足も速く、団牌と飛刀、投槍を使う好漢だった。項充と似た技を備え、丸い盾に飛刀をびっしり差し、背には投槍を隠し持った。戦場では盾を旋風のように舞わせ、数歩ないし丈を隔てた敵へ刃や槍を投げて傷つけた。とりわけ走り跳ぶことに優れ、乱軍の中を飛ぶように往来して突き進む速さは、まるで雲や霧に乗っているかのようだった。その軽快さと神速の動きから江湖で「飛天大聖」と呼ばれ、まさしく風のように現れては去る、捉え難い男だった。

李袞と項充の交情は非常に厚かった。二人とも徐州、邳州一帯の命知らずの好漢で、罪を犯して居場所を失い、ともに芒碭山へ向かい、妖術を使う混世魔王樊瑞の配下に加わった。樊瑞を首領とし、項充と李袞が左右の副将となって、三人は芒碭山に拠り、命知らずを集め、家々を襲って略奪した。樊瑞には風雨を呼ぶ妖術があり、二人の副将には団牌と飛刀の絶技があったため、その勢力と名声は大いに高まった。やがて梁山泊を併呑して水滸の基盤を奪う野心を抱き、山を攻めると公言したことから、梁山との争いを招いた。

三人の大言を聞いた宋江は兵馬を集め、自ら芒碭山へ遠征した。同行した公孫勝は、樊瑞の術は邪道にすぎず、五雷の正法で破れると述べた。両軍が対陣すると、李袞と項充が先頭に出て、それぞれ団牌を舞わせながら地を転がるように進み、飛刀と投槍を一斉に放って宋江の陣へ攻め込んだ。左右に風車のように旋回する勢いは鋭く、あやうく宋公明を傷つけるところまで迫った。幸い呂方と郭盛が二本の戟をそろえて必死に防ぎ、公孫勝も密かに術を施して落とし穴を用意していた。戦いに夢中になった李袞と項充は足元を警戒せず、ともに穴へ落ち、伏兵の鉤と縄で生け捕りにされて陣幕へ送られた。

二人の並外れた勇気を見た宋江は害するに忍びず、自ら縄を解き、幕内へ招き、酒を振る舞って優しく慰めた。天に代わって道を行い、義をもって賢者を集めたいという心を語り、帰順を勧めた。率直な二人は、宋江が礼を尽くし少しも害意を持たないことに感動し、ひれ伏して降り、喜んで仲間となった。さらに自ら芒碭山へ戻り、樊瑞を説得すると申し出た。山へ帰ると、宋公明の仁義と恩徳を詳しく伝えた。その後、樊瑞は公孫勝と術を競い、妖術をことごとく正法に破られて、ようやく心から服した。項充と李袞の懸命な説得もあり、芒碭山の全軍を率いて梁山泊へ帰順した。以来、三人は水滸の大寨で肝胆相照らし、二度と離れることはなかった。

聚義の席次が定まると、李袞は地走星、第六十五位に列し、項充と肩を並べる歩軍頭領となった。二人とも団牌と飛刀を得意とし、先駆けて敵陣を破り、防備を突破するのに最も向いていた。苦しい激戦ではしばしば真っ先に突入して敵陣を乱す、梁山歩軍でも並ぶ者のない勇猛な先鋒の一組であった。その後の遼国、田虎、王慶の征討でも、李袞は勇んで先頭を争い、たびたび戦功を挙げた。親友の項充とは常に影のように連れ添い、肩を並べて敵と戦った。

方臘征討の江南の戦いは、何にも増して凄惨だった。大軍が歙州に進むと、李袞と項充はいつものように歩軍を率いて先陣を切ったが、思いがけず敵の伏兵にはまった。山道は険しく狭いため、団牌や飛刀の技を十分に発揮できず、二人は重囲に陥って進退に窮した。李袞は死力を尽くして戦ったものの、多勢には抗しきれず、乱軍の刀槍の下に命を落として戦場に殉じた。生涯、飛ぶように走り、盾を舞わせて敵陣を破り、向かうところ敵のなかった「飛天大聖」も、ついに江南の険地で力尽きた。生死を共にした項充と同じ戦役で倒れ、軍が凱旋する日を見ることはなかった。芒碭で義を結び、共に梁山へ上り、共に各地へ出征し、最後には同じ場所で死んだ二人は、生死を通じて一度も志を変えなかった。その義の深さと最期の激しさは、水滸の諸将の悲壮な結末の中でもひときわ胸を打ち、義のために命を捨てたこの兄弟を思う後人は、涙を浮かべて嘆息するのである。
